title: Suspects charged in brazen train heist ring that netted $22 million in cargo from major retailers
summary: Authorities have charged more than a dozen people for allegedly orchestrating a massive train heist operation
story: Authorities have charged more than a dozen people for allegedly orchestrating a massive train heist operation

LOS ANGELES -- More than a dozen people were charged Thursday with allegedly orchestrating a massive train heist operation to steal over $22 million in cargo — from popular shoes to power tools — from major retailers.

A federal indictment unsealed on Thursday paints a picture of an organized group that targeted more than three dozen trains carrying Nike sneakers, Crocs footwear, power tools and other consumer goods that were imported into the United States through Los Angeles and Long Beach, which are home to the busiest ports in the country.

Trains that shuttle goods to stores and customers around the country have become a prominent target for large-scale theft in recent years, especially at large ports in the U.S. that receive hundreds of millions of dollars of shipments every day. The relatively low-tech robberies have demanded attention from the world's largest retailers, including the likes of Amazon.

The men would disable the trains at a planned location by busting the brakes, the indictment alleged, at which point the goods would be offloaded onto trucks. The goods were then peddled to an unnamed company that would resell the stolen merchandise for profit.
“The scale of the theft is staggering,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli, promising to prosecute any future efforts to steal the merchandise.

In group chats, the men shared numerous photos and videos of themselves busting into the hulking train cars, and posing with wads of cash and stolen merchandise. They also shared AI photos of themselves captioned “Los Trenes,” which means the trains in Spanish, beneath glamorized photos of men throwing boxes of shoes off trains into nearby cars while police helicopters descended overhead.
The 13 men were indicted for conspiracy and theft of interstate railroad cargo. Two were also charged with violence against railroad carriers.
If convicted, the men could face anywhere from five to 20 years in federal prison.

title: Average US 30-year mortgage rate rises to 7.28% this week, ending a four-week slide
summary: The average long-term U.S. mortgage rate rose this week for the first time since early October, reflecting a ramp-up in U.S. government bond yields amid signs that inflation is heating up
story: The average long-term U.S. mortgage rate rose this week for the first time since early October, reflecting a ramp-up in U.S. government bond yields amid signs that inflation is heating up
The average long-term U.S. mortgage rate rose this week for the first time since early October, reflecting a ramp-up in U.S. government bond yields amid signs that inflation is heating up.
The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage in the U.S. rose to 7.28% from 7.11% last week, mortgage buyer Freddie Mac said Thursday. One year ago, the average rate was 6.26%.
The average rate eased in the four weeks heading into this week and hadn't increased since Oct. 8, when it hit 7.40%, its highest level in nearly three years.

Higher mortgage rates can add hundreds of dollars a month in costs for borrowers, limiting homebuyers’ purchasing power at a time when affordability challenges continue to sideline many aspiring homeowners.

Borrowing costs on 15-year fixed-rate mortgages, often sought by borrowers refinancing a home loan, also rose this week. That average rate climbed to 6.66% from 6.45% last week. A year ago, it was at 5.54%.

Rates on home loans are influenced by inflation, Federal Reserve policy and bond-market investors’ expectations for the economy, among other factors. They generally follow the trajectory of the 10-year Treasury yield, which lenders use as a guide to pricing home loans.

That yield had been mostly trending lower since early October, after climbing to its highest level since 2002, but it has been rising again following new data showing hotter inflation. The 10-year Treasury yield was at 5.05% at midday on the bond market Thursday.

The signs pointing to accelerating inflation have raised the odds that the Federal Reserve will hike its key interest rate at its next meeting in December. The central bank kept rates unchanged late last month, after raising them in September.
While the Fed doesn’t set mortgage rates, its decisions to raise or lower its short-term rate are watched closely by bond investors and can ultimately influence rates on home loans.

“The debate has shifted from whether the Fed hikes in December to how aggressively it moves,” said Anthony Smith, a senior economist at Realtor.com. “That is a tough backdrop for mortgage rates heading into what is already a seasonally slow stretch for the housing market.”
Mortgage rates have been marching higher overall since late February, when the U.S. war with Iran began, pushing up the price of oil and driving inflation higher.

In late February, the average rate on a 30-year mortgage briefly dipped to 5.98%, its lowest level going back to late 2022. Going by the latest average rate, a home shopper financing a $400,000 home loan is now paying roughly $343 more a month than when the rate was just below 6%.

Elevated home loan borrowing costs have weighed on home sales this year, deepening a national housing slump that dates back to 2022, when mortgage rates began to climb from pandemic-era lows. Sales of previously occupied U.S. homes were essentially flat last year, stuck at a 30-year low. They declined last month to their slowest annual pace in more than 16 years as mortgage rates surged.
And the latest monthly tally of home purchase transactions that have yet to be finalized points to potentially more sluggish home sales in coming months.

Pending U.S. home sales fell 4.7% last month from September and sank 16.7% from October last year, the National Association of Realtors said Wednesday. There’s usually a month or two lag between a contract signing and when the sale is finalized, which makes pending home sales a near-term bellwether for the housing market.

title: A rare EU-UK summit as Andy Burnham seeks to mend Brexit damage
summary: A decade after Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences and possibly pave a way to get back together
story: A decade after Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences and possibly pave a way to get back together

BRUSSELS -- A decade after the people of Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences, and just perhaps, to pave the way for them to get back together.

Burnham is scheduled to hold just under an hour of talks in Brussels with European Council President António Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Then they'll all meet in a plenary session with U.K. government ministers and European commissioners.

Burnham has described the rare EU-U.K. summit — only the second since Britain became the first country to leave the world’s biggest trading bloc — as a step toward undoing a decade of damage caused by the divorce.
“The Brexit we were given has not worked. We have lost more than we gained,” he said this week.

Burnham has said all options should be on the table for future relations, including rejoining the now-27-nation bloc. But he's stressed that reversing Brexit is just one possible outcome, and far from imminent. It would need the backing not just of British voters, but the unanimous support of a mistrustful EU. Still, he has broken a long political code of silence on the option of rejoining.

Ahead of the meeting, von der Leyen said she wanted it to be “a summit of ambition and concrete results. More opportunities for young people. Easier agrifood trade. And a stronger cooperation on economic security.”

The two sides are expected to sign a trade deal for food and drink, an agreement on emissions trading and a plan to let young people work for limited periods across Britain and the EU. Burnham says the deals could add a modest 0.4% to Britain’s economy.

The war in Ukraine, and the U.K.’s military strength, are drawing the two back together, and the summit provides the EU with an opportunity to discuss stronger cooperation on security and defense, as well as efforts to restrict irregular migration.

“Our security and prosperity are closely intertwined, making a strong partnership between us essential,” Costa said ahead of the meeting. “By deepening our cooperation, we can strengthen our ability to address the challenges of our time, strengthen our resilience and promote stability in Europe and beyond.”

Nevertheless, feelings remain raw, and EU officials have been reluctant to encourage talk of the U.K. rejoining. They are weary from the shifting demands of seven British prime ministers over the last decade and want real clarity about the country’s intentions.

Ireland’s ambassador in London, Sonja Hyland, said that when Britain voted for Brexit, “there was a lack of clarity as to exactly what that meant.” If Britain wants to reopen negotiations, she said, it must “make a clear decision as to what it wants.”
Lawless reported from London.

title: Kenya picks US consortium for critical minerals project as residents seek answers
summary: Kenya’s government has selected a consortium of U.S. companies to develop niobium and rare earths deposits on its coast
story: Kenya’s government has selected a consortium of U.S. companies to develop niobium and rare earths deposits on its coast

NAIROBI, Kenya -- Kenya’s government said Thursday that it had selected a consortium of U.S. companies as the preferred bidder to develop niobium and rare earths deposits on its coast, while residents said they were still waiting for information on the project.

The mining ministry said it had issued a notice of its intention to award the Mrima Hill project in Kwale County to the Frontier Minerals Consortium, which comprises Frontier Minerals LLC, Bunker Hill Mining Corp., ReElement Technologies and American Resources Corp.

The ministry stressed that the notice is not a license. It said the consortium must now “go to the ground,” engage communities and obtain “all requisite consents” before applying for a prospecting license.

Residents and farmers have told The Associated Press that they fear losing their land. Elders from the local Digo community worry about damage to a sacred forest where they say their ancestors are buried.

“Until now, we have received no information from the government on the content of the project,” said Justus Mwero, chairman of the Mrima Farm Owners Community-Based Organization. “It will be hard for us to express our consent or opinion to the company with no information.”
Countries including the U.S. are racing to secure the rare earth minerals used in electric vehicle motors, wind turbines and defense technologies, seeking alternatives to China’s dominance.
The ministry said it had “deliberately” chosen investors before starting formal consent processes. Mining Minister Hassan Joho told the AP on Nov. 2 the community was consulted before seeking bids.

“The government should make the proposal public, so that the company can be held accountable. The government should not distance themselves from their responsibilities and leave it to the investor,” said Fakii Omar of the Kwale Mining Alliance.
The Mrima Hill Sacred Grove was designated a national monument in 1992.
“The notice does not mention if the protected status of the forest has been revoked," Omar added. "Can the proposed mine coexist with the protected status under current laws?”

A previous attempt to mine the site ended in arbitration. In 2013, Kenya’s environment regulator rejected an environmental assessment for a license held by Cortec Mining Kenya, citing the site’s protected status, according to Extractives Daily. An arbitration tribunal of the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes later ruled that the license should not have been issued without environmental approval, and Kenya won the case.

The Centre for Litigation Trust, a Kenyan civil society group, has asked the High Court in Kwale County to suspend a proposed Kenya-U.S. agreement on Mrima Hill’s minerals until residents are consulted. The attorney general has challenged the court’s jurisdiction.

title: Trump wants Supreme Court to let EPA cancel billions in Biden-era climate grants
summary: The Trump administration is appealing to the Supreme Court in its push to cut $16 billion in grants for a climate program
story: The Trump administration is appealing to the Supreme Court in its push to cut $16 billion in grants for a climate program

WASHINGTON -- The Trump administration is appealing to the Supreme Court in its push to cut $16 billion in grants for a climate program, the largest grant cancellation case ever and one that could affect Republican President Donald Trump's push to defund the priorities of prior administrations.
The justices have not said whether they will take the case.

If they do, it could resolve a fight over grants that the Environmental Protection Agency rescinded in 2025. Democratic President Joe Biden's administration awarded the money under a 2022 law to finance clean energy projects and accelerate the transition from fossil fuels. Trump has targeted other grants, such as those considered to be supporting diversity, equity and inclusion. A favorable outcome at the high court could help his administration defeat other grant lawsuits, according to the government's filing this month.

At issue is the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund, commonly referred to as a “green bank." Climate United Fund and other nonprofits were picked to operate the program authorized by the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act. If the justices decline to take the case, the groups could regain access to their money because a federal appeals court already ruled in their favor.
The EPA canceled the nonprofits' grants soon after the start of Trump’s second term in January 2025, with EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin accusing the groups of mismanagement and potential fraud.

The nonprofits' lawsuit argues that the EPA broke the law and violated the Constitution. It demands access to their grant money so they can run the program. The administration says it is immune from legal and constitutional claims and contends the groups filed their case in the wrong court.

If the justices eventually side with the EPA, it could "have far-reaching implications for the government’s ability to reshape grant programs and to terminate grants that do not advance a particular administration’s policy priorities,” said Romany Webb, deputy director of the Sabin Center for Climate Change Law at Columbia University who has supported Climate United’s arguments.
The EPA says the $16 billion at stake is the largest grant cancellation case ever and is another reason it warrants Supreme Court review.
The courts have so far tried to thwart the administration's priorities, the EPA wrote in its petition to the Supreme Court.
The EPA and Climate United declined to comment.

In August, a divided federal appeals court in Washington sided with the nonprofits and said the administration improperly terminated the grants. The release of any money was paused to give the Supreme Court a chance to weigh in.
The justices ruled for the administration recently in decisions over canceled National Institutes of Health grants and teacher training grants.

The administration has built its arguments around the Tucker Act, which gives the Court of Federal Claims exclusive authority over contract disputes. The claims court can award money, but not direct the government to take certain actions in the way federal courts can.

The nonprofits argued the way the EPA canceled the grants did not upend a contract with the federal government, but was done illegally and undercut spending on entire programs Congress had required, a constitutional violation. The government argues the matter is a contract dispute.

The administration’s broad use of contract cancellations to enact policies is a novel approach, according to Bob Wagman, president of the Court of Federal Claims Bar Association and a partner at the firm White & Case.

“I would hate to think that the only programs that could be supported have a four-year life,” he said, mentioning cancer research as an example of a grant program that would need longer than a single administration to pay off. “It is just not good for the country.”
Zeldin last year told Fox News that he suspected the green bank “was a clear-cut case of waste and abuse.”

U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan said that when the government was asked for evidence of fraud, the EPA did not provide it and shifted its position to more general concerns about the level of oversight over the program. Chutkan said the government cannot terminate the contracts in violation of the law and that the groups should have access to some of their frozen money, which is held in an account at Citibank.
The administration has been adamant that nothing requires them to make these grants to these groups.

Passage of the Inflation Reduction Act created the green bank. Trump’s tax and spending bill passed last year rescinded part of the law that established the bank and the money that had not already been obligated to its recipients. The EPA has said that those changes mean it should not have to release any money to the groups.
Associated Press writer Jennifer McDermott in Providence, R.I., contributed to this report.

title: Walmart raises its outlook for the year for the 3rd time after a solid quarter
summary: Walmart reported solid sales for the fiscal quarter as the discounter continues to attract a growing number of customers across the economic spectrum seeking to cut costs in the face of rising prices
story: Walmart reported solid sales for the fiscal quarter as the discounter continues to attract a growing number of customers across the economic spectrum seeking to cut costs in the face of rising prices

NEW YORK -- Walmart reported solid third quarter sales gains as the retailer continues to attract a growing number of customers across the economic spectrum that are seeking to cut costs in the face of rising prices.

The company topped Wall Street’s profit and sales projections, and it raised its annual guidance for the third time this year, but the outlook released Thursday was more conservative than industry analysts had expected.

Comparable sales, which include digital channels and stores, rose 2.9%. That is better than last quarter's 2.6% increase, when Walmart reported its weakest comparable sales growth in six years. But it's still a slowdown from the 4.5% growth registered during the same period last year.

Still, slowing comparable sales, particularly in Walmart stores, also reflect a strategic shift toward e-commerce, Walmart+ memberships and advertising. Global e-commerce sales rose 17%, while U.S. e-commerce sales increased 23% during the latest quarter, the company said.

Walmart said that more than 80% of U.S. e-commerce orders are being fulfilled from stores, including its third party marketplace orders. Stores enabled faster delivery speeds on a wide range of assortments, the retailer said.
Shares rose nearly 1% before the opening bell Thursday.

“We delivered strong results, growing our core business and gaining market share,” Walmart's CEO John Furner said in prepared remarks. “The strength of our omnichannel model gives us room to do even more.”

Walmart is considered a barometer of consumer spending given its vast customer base. More than 150 million customers use its website or visit its stores every week, according to Walmart. Analysts look to the massive retailer for clues about what to expect from the industry as a whole during the critical holiday shopping season.

Consumers in the U.S. have remained resilient in the face of painful inflation, but they have also grown more selective about what they buy. Many rely on retailers like Walmart as a one-stop shop for low-priced household goods, groceries and pharmaceuticals.

The latest U.S. retail sales data revealed that shoppers increased spending more slowly in October as Americans pulled back on a variety of purchases, from cars, clothing and furniture and even their own hobbies.
Retail sales rose 0.2% in October, down from a 0.8% gain in September, according to Commerce Department data released this week.
Walmart has been hammering its low price message while refining its store label fashion brands like Scoop and Free Assembly.

Walmart is also trying to increase subscriptions to its shipping programs. During the third quarter, Walmart launched a combined Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus annual membership bundle for $120 per year. The package saves shoppers nearly $100 compared to buying both plans separately, it said.

Walmart, based in Bentonville, Arkansas, has begun to capture a larger share of wealthier consumers. The biggest gains in market share for Walmart have been coming from households with annual incomes over $100,000, the retailer has said.

Walmart’s quarterly net income was $4.94 billion, or 62 cents per share, in the three-month period ended Oct. 31. Adjusted per-share results were 65 cents, higher than the 64 cents Wall Street had expected, according to FactSet. In the year-ago quarter, the company earned $6.14 billion, or 77 cents per share.
Sales rose 5.2% to $188.8 billion in the latest quarter. Analysts were predicting $187.38 billion, according to FactSet.

The company said that comparable sales were driven by groceries and general merchandise categories like furniture and toys. But the figure was once again hit by federal legislation that requires pharmacies to dispense some high-cost Medicare drugs at capped prices, the retailer said.

For the full year, Walmart now projects earnings per share to be in the range of $2.84 to $2.89, up from the prior guidance of $2.80 to $2.87. Sales should be up anywhere from 4.9% to 5.2%, up from the prior forecast of 4% to 5%. That would mean a forecast for sales in the range of $748.12 billion to $750.25 billion, according to FactSet.
Analysts expected $2.89 per share and sales of $752.68 billion for the year, according to FactSet.

title: Japan's PM Takaichi says Russia and Japan will keep talking as ties remain chilled
summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi says that she met with Russian President Vladimir Putin for more than 30 minutes in the first such encounter between the two countries’ leaders in seven years
story: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi says that she met with Russian President Vladimir Putin for more than 30 minutes in the first such encounter between the two countries’ leaders in seven years

SHENZHEN, China -- Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Thursday that she and Russian President Vladimir Putin held talks and agreed to keep communicating in the first such encounter between the two countries’ leaders in seven years.

Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, she said she raised the issue of Moscow’s treatment of Japanese businesses in Russia and urged Putin to release a Japanese journalist detained for alleged spying during their meeting late Wednesday in Shenzhen, China.
“We reached an agreement to maintain communication at various levels, including direct contact between the president and myself,” Takaichi said.
Japan's ties with Russia have long been strained by a territorial dispute dating back decades.

Japan lodged a protest with Russia in October over the arrest of a Japanese journalist working for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper on suspicion of spying, demanding that Moscow provide an explanation, consular access and humane treatment.

Moscow recently seized control of some local subsidiaries of Japan Tobacco, the largest cigarette maker in Russia, and the company reported it expects a 724 billion yen ($4.5 billion) loss for this year due to the takeover.

Earlier, Japan Tobacco had forecast a 662 billion yen profit for the financial year ending Dec. 31. The company said it has not given up legal ownership of the Russia-based subsidiaries or withdrawn from operating in Russia.

Tensions rose in August after Putin visited Iturup, one of four Russian-controlled islands off Japan’s northern coast that Tokyo also claims. Earlier this month, Tokyo protested after two Russian aircraft briefly violated Japanese airspace off southwestern Japan.

The last bilateral in-person talks between Japanese and Russian leaders were held between then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and Putin in September 2019, during the Eastern Economic Forum in the Russian city of Vladivostok.

Putin is attending the annual APEC summit for the first time in nine years. He, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump held a summit meeting Thursday after the APEC gathering, an event that seems to underscore Japan's diminished role as a global power.
Takaichi herself was given a very minimal reception on her arrival in Shenzhen, provoking speculation over a deliberate snub by her hosts.
When asked, Takaichi said she did not believe the summit between Xi, Trump and Putin would undermine Japan’s interests.

“We have been maintaining close communication with the United States and other allies while carefully monitoring the impact on the international situation and we will continue to respond appropriately,” Takaichi said. "We do not believe that Japan’s interests will be compromised.”
She did not elaborate on efforts to repair damage to Japan’s ties with China following remarks she made nearly a year ago about Taiwan.
“China is an important neighbor. Given the various issues and challenges that exist between Japan and China, I believe it is essential to engage in dialogue and maintain communication," she said.
Yamaguchi reported from Tokyo. Associated Press journalist Haruka Nuga in Tokyo contributed to this report.

title: Wall Street tumbles to its longest losing streak since 2024 as the Dow drops 1,100 points
summary: The U.S. stock market tumbled again as AI stocks kept falling on worries their boom may be over
story: The U.S. stock market tumbled again as AI stocks kept falling on worries their boom may be over

NEW YORK -- The U.S. stock market tumbled again as beaten-down stocks tied to artificial intelligence kept falling Thursday on worries their breathtaking boom may be over. The losses came even though a leading AI lab, Anthropic, found a strong welcome for the debut of its own stock on Wall Street.

The S&P 500 dropped 2% for a sixth straight loss. That’s its longest losing streak in two and a half years, and the index at the heart of many 401(k) accounts is now down 8.2% from its all-time high set last month.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,101 points, or 2.2%, while the Nasdaq composite sank 2.3%.
The losses were widespread, and more than 90% of the stocks that make up the S&P 500 index fell.

Leading them downward was Williams-Sonoma, which dropped 15.2% after the company behind Pottery Barn and West Elm reported revenue for the latest quarter that was a bit weaker than Wall Street expected. It also stuck with its forecast for how much revenue it will make throughout 2026, and the midpoint of that range was below what analysts were expecting.
Walmart sank 1% even though it reported profit and revenue for the latest quarter that edged past analysts’ expectations.
For a while Thursday morning, gains for several AI-related stocks seemed to be enough to more than make up for such losses.

The S&P 500 jumped as much as 1.3% after Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, sold shares of its stock at $83 apiece in its initial public offering. That’s more than the $70 to $78 it earlier thought it would get, and its price quickly surged above $115 after it began trading on the Nasdaq shortly before noon.
Anthropic later pared its gain and finished the day at $97.17, still up 17.1%.

Even before its stock began trading, the strong demand for Anthropic’s IPO appeared to demonstrate faith remained among investors in the AI revolution. The industry needed a boost following sharp recent drops for AI-related stocks on worries their prices shot too high in the frenzy around the technology.
But AI stocks quickly returned to their jittery ways in what Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives, called “a very turbulent, white-knuckle period.”
Micron Technology, whose sales of memory for computers have soared because of the AI boom, initially rallied 7.8% and then swung to a loss of 2.1%.
CoreWeave, a company that buys AI chips and rents out access to them to customers over the cloud, went from a 10.5% leap in the morning to a drop of 6.1%.
Nvidia erased its early gain of 4.7% and flipped to a loss of 3.3% amid the lengthening list of worries dogging the entire industry.

At first it was criticism that AI stocks had broadly gone into a bubble after shooting so high, along with doubts that AI could produce enough profit and productivity to make the massive investments in data centers worth it. Then it was worries that high interest rates would mean less borrowed money to fund the industry’s growth. Then came this month’s sweeping victories for Democrats in the U.S. midterm elections, which raised concerns about more regulation for AI.

Most recently, it was the sudden resignation of Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s CEO. He was one of AI’s biggest evangelists and helped build interest in the industry while using some of Nvidia’s massive profits to further fund its growth.
Other companies, meanwhile, offered more encouraging signals about AI.

Palo Alto Networks climbed 6.4% after the AI cybersecurity company topped analysts’ expectations for profit and revenue in the latest quarter. It also agreed to buy Applied Compute, a platform for post-training and inference of open-weight AI models, to help customers adopt AI securely. The all-stock deal is valued at $4.5 billion.

Everpure, a company that helps businesses manage and store their data, said its revenue jumped last quarter by more than analysts expected in part because of AI-related offerings. Everpure’s stock rose 4.7%.
All told, the S&P 500 fell 147.80 points to 7,175.83. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,101.11 to 49,097.06, and the Nasdaq composite sank 550.69 to 23,879.20.

In the bond market, Treasury yields eased as the drops for stock prices sent investors toward investments seen as safer. When prices for Treasury bonds go up, their yields go down, and the yield on the 10-year Treasury fell to 5.04% from 5.07% Wednesday.

Also weighing on yields were a couple reports on the U.S. economy that came in weaker than economists expected. One said slightly more U.S. workers applied for unemployment benefits last week, though the number remains low compared with history. Another said manufacturing growth in the mid-Atlantic region is slowing by more than economists expected.

In stock markets abroad, Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 0.7%. Helping to lead the way was SoftBank Group, which climbed 4.6%. It was an early investor in OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT and competitor to Anthropic.
South Korea’s Kospi climbed 1.4% thanks to strength for its stocks tied to the AI boom, but stocks were weaker elsewhere in Asia and in Europe. Germany’s DAX lost 1.1%.
AP Business Writer Chan Ho-him contributed to this report.

title: Pant reaches 100 as India tightens its control on the 1st test against New Zealand
summary: Rishabh Pant has completed a dashing century before falling one ball from lunch as India tightened its grip on the first cricket test against New Zealand in the morning session on the fourth day
story: Rishabh Pant has completed a dashing century before falling one ball from lunch as India tightened its grip on the first cricket test against New Zealand in the morning session on the fourth day

WELLINGTON, New Zealand -- Rishabh Pant completed a dashing century before falling one ball from lunch Sunday as India tightened its grip on the first cricket test against New Zealand in the morning session on the fourth day.
India was 629-6 at the break, a lead of 261 runs over New Zealand's first innings of 368. Pant was dismissed for 128, leaving Dhruv Jurel not out on 32.

Pant began the day on 52 and compiled his ninth test century from 135 balls with nine fours and four sixes. He went from 99 to 105 with a six from the spin bowling of Glenn Phillips, highlighting the daring and unorthodoxy of his batting approach.
The century was his fourth since his return to test cricket in 2024 after a devastating car accident.
Pant put 68 runs in the first hour Sunday with Anshul Kamboj before the nightwatchman's good contribution was halted at 38 when he was caught by Devon Conway off Phillips.

Pant's 68-run stand with Kamboj continued the run of substantial partnerships among the India top order, following K.L Rahul's 130 for the first wicket with Yashasvi Jaiswal; 165 for the second wicket between Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal; 91 for the third wicket between Rahul and India captain Shubman Gill and 100 between Gill and Pant.
Jaiswal made 85 and Gill was out for 98 two balls before stumps on the third day.

Pant delights in the contest with bowlers and fielders, happily taking on the boundary riders of which New Zealand had five Sunday. His wagon wheel shows his impressive range of shots; three sixes down the ground, others behind square and his boundaries mostly through the leg side. He deployed as usual his odd, off-balance reverse sweep.
He provided the impetus as India added 143 runs in 27 overs before lunch.
Of the New Zealand bowlers, Jacob Duffy came in for most punishment, conceding 201 runs from his 33 overs.

title: Fletcher's 3 TD runs lift No. 5 Miami past Virginia Tech 28-20, 'Canes clinch spot in ACC title game
summary: Mark Fletcher Jr. rushed for three touchdowns, Jake Weinberg kicked the longest field goal in Miami history and the fifth-ranked Hurricanes erased a 14-point deficit to beat Virginia Tech 28-20 on Saturday night and clinch a spot in the Atlantic Coast ...
story: Mark Fletcher Jr. rushed for three touchdowns, Jake Weinberg kicked the longest field goal in Miami history and the fifth-ranked Hurricanes erased a 14-point deficit to beat Virginia Tech 28-20 on Saturday night and clinch a spot in the Atlantic Coast ...

MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Mark Fletcher Jr. rushed for three touchdowns, Jake Weinberg kicked the longest field goal in Miami history and the fifth-ranked Hurricanes erased a 14-point deficit to beat Virginia Tech 28-20 on Saturday night and clinch a spot in the Atlantic Coast Conference title game.

Fletcher had the second three-touchdown game of his career for Miami (10-1, 8-0 ACC, No. 7 CFP), while Cooper Barkate and Vandrevius Jacobs combined on 14 catches for 132 yards for the Hurricanes — who will face Wake Forest for the ACC title in Charlotte, North Carolina, on Dec. 5.

Weinberg connected on a school-record, 59-yard field goal to end the first half. The previous record was 57, done by three kickers: Danny Miller in 1981, Michael Badgley in 2015 and Jose Borregales in 2020.

Ethan Grunkemeyer completed 22 of 35 passes for 168 yards for Virginia Tech (6-5, 3-5), which lost to Miami for the sixth consecutive time. The Hokies led 20-14 lead entering the fourth quarter before Fletcher scored on the first play of the final stanza to give Miami its first lead of the night.
Fletcher scored from 11 yards out with 2:08 left to push the lead to eight, and Miami took the ball over on downs with 1:27 remaining.
Miami, which got 241 passing yards from Darian Mensah and played again without injured receiver Malachi Toney, was in big trouble from the outset.

Virginia Tech won the opening toss and elected to receive. Someone in the coin-flip huddle yelled “noooo” after a Hokies' captain told referee Garrett Dickerson that they wanted the football, though it wasn't clear if the visitors actually wanted to defer to the second half.
Either way, it worked out — at least, for a while.
The Hokies went 75 yards in 15 plays on the game's first drive, Grunkemeyer connecting with Jeffrey Overton Jr. for a five-yard touchdown pass to open the scoring.
And three plays later, it was 14-0.

Mensah's first interception of the night was a ball that skipped off Miami running back Javian Mallory's hands and was picked off by the Hokies' Joshua Clarke. An unsportsmanlike conduct penalty on Mallory advanced the ball to the Miami 15, and Messiah Mickens went in from there one play later to give the Hokies a two-touchdown lead.
Weinberg made it 14-3 with a 49-yard field goal, and Fletcher's first TD of the night — combined with a 2-point conversion — made it 14-11.

Virginia Tech: The Hokies wasted a 14-point lead for the second time this season, after also doing so against Pitt in what became a 35-33 loss on Oct. 2. Virginia Tech had been 50-3 in its last 53 games with 14-point leads before Saturday night.
Miami: The Hurricanes have now won 12 consecutive ACC games, the longest such run in school history. The last time Miami had an 11-game ACC winning streak, it was snapped — by Virginia Tech.
Virginia Tech: Hosts Virginia next Saturday.
Miami: Hosts Boston College next Saturday.

title: Lamar survives to beat McNeese 19-17; earns share of Southland title and automatic berth to playoffs
summary: Andres Sandoval kicked four field goals, including the game winner with 13 seconds remaining, and Lamar survived an upset bid from McNeese, beating the Cowboys 19-17 to close out the regular season
story: Andres Sandoval kicked four field goals, including the game winner with 13 seconds remaining, and Lamar survived an upset bid from McNeese, beating the Cowboys 19-17 to close out the regular season

LAKE CHARLES, La. -- Andres Sandoval kicked four field goals, including the game winner with 13 seconds remaining, and Lamar survived an upset bid from McNeese on Saturday, beating the Cowboys 19-17 to close out the regular season.

The Cardinals (10-2, 8-1 Southland Conference), ranked No. 4 in the Stats Perform FCS poll, clinched a share of the conference title with fifth-ranked Stephen F. Austin. Lamar earned the automatic postseason berth by beating the Lumberjacks 45-28 earlier this month.
Lamar's lone touchdown came when Parker Jenkins bulled his way into the end zone from a yard out for a 7-0 lead.
Brady Barrier answered with a 27-yard touchdown pass to Elisha Edwards to tie it 7-7 after one quarter.

Sandoval kicked a 20-yard field goal for the lone score of the second quarter and a 10-7 lead. He kicked a 24-yarder for the only points in the third, then connected from 38-yards out with 7:37 remaining for a 16-7 lead.
Barrier and Edwards teamed up again for a 24-yard touchdown and Deagian Camron kicked a 36-yard field goal with 1:23 left to put the Cowboys (5-7, 4-5) up a point.
Aiden McCown connected with Davin Driskell for a 34-yard gain on first down for Lamar. McCown passed 13 yards to Blake Thomas and then hit Driskell for 6 more to set up Sandoval's winning kick.
LaDamion McDowell finished with 105 yards on 17 carries for the Cardinals.
Barrier totaled 164 yards on 13-for-18 passing for McNeese. Edwards had five catches for 78 yards, and Omiri Wiggins rushed 17 times for 125 yards.

title: Murray's putback with 5 seconds left lifts Kings to 97-96 win over Celtics and end 8-game skid
summary: Keegan Murray’s putback over three defenders with 5 seconds left gave the Sacramento Kings a 97-96 win over the Boston Celtics on Saturday
story: Keegan Murray’s putback over three defenders with 5 seconds left gave the Sacramento Kings a 97-96 win over the Boston Celtics on Saturday
SACRAMENTO, Calif. -- Keegan Murray's putback over three defenders with 5 seconds left lifted the Sacramento Kings to a 97-96 victory over the Boston Celtics on Saturday.
The Kings snapped an eight-game losing streak and earned their first home win this season following the back-and-forth game down the stretch.
Trailing by one with 11.8 seconds left, Darius Acuff Jr. drove the lane and his shot was off. Murray grabbed the putback and scored to give the Kings the one-point advantage.
Payton Pritchard had a chance to win it at the buzzer, but his 20-footer was off.
All five Kings starters reached double-figure scoring and were led by Acuff Jr.'s 21 points, six rebounds and eight assists. Murray added 15 points and 12 rebounds.
Jayson Tatum (rest), Derrick White (shoulder) and Mitchell Robinson (illness) did not play against Sacramento, leaving Boston undermanned going into the matchup.
The Celtics' defense suffocated the Kings early on, forcing multiple turnovers and vaulted Boston to an early 10-0 lead to start the game.

It looked like Sacramento was on its way to a ninth straight loss entering the second half down 54-41. The Kings' defense, which ranks among the bottom of the league in opponent points per game at 120.7, held the Celtics well below that.
A 35-13 third quarter in favor of Sacramento was the difference maker, as Boston missed all 13 of its 3-point attempts in the period. The Celtics took 58 3-pointers on the game and only shot 22%.
Sacramento took a 76-67 lead into the fourth quarter, but the Celtics fought back. Pritchard hit a step back shot to put Celtics up 96-95 with 11.8 seconds to go.
Paul George scored 19 points to lead the Celtics.
Celtics: Visit Golden State on Sunday.
Kings: Host San Antonio on Monday.

title: Jets score on first 5 drives and edge Chargers 27-24 to snap 5-game skid
summary: Geno Smith led the New York Jets to a 27-24 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers, ending a five-game losing streak
story: Geno Smith led the New York Jets to a 27-24 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers, ending a five-game losing streak

INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Geno Smith completed 17 of 21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns, including two to Sterling Shepard, and the New York Jets scored on their first five drives to beat the Los Angeles Chargers 27-24 on Sunday and end a five-game skid.

Smith connected with Breece Hall for a 7-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter, snapping a 10-quarter streak without a TD over three games and giving the Jets a 10-3 lead. The score coincided with offensive coordinator Frank Reich's move from the booth to the field to call plays for the first time this season.
Smith showed no ill effects after being limited in practice earlier in the week as the result of hurting his left ankle in a loss to Buffalo last weekend.
Shepard caught two TD passes for the first time in his career after being elevated from the practice squad on Saturday.

The Jets (3-8) got their second road win of the season and also ended a five-game losing streak against the Chargers (1-9). New York had never scored on every possession in a game in their history, but didn't need to on their sixth and last drive in this one when Braelon Allen ran for 15 on third-and-7 to seal the win.
Jets rookie David Bailey had two sacks, giving him 9 1/2 on the season to go with six forced fumbles, including one against the Chargers.
Los Angeles was coming off its first win of the season at Baltimore on Monday, but trailed the entire game in falling to 0-5 at SoFi Stadium.

The Bolts closed to 27-23 on Justin Herbert's 6-yard TD pass to Ladd McConkey — their second connection of the game — with 1:58 remaining in the fourth. It was the first time in 11 games that Herbert had multiple TDs in a game dating to last season.

Herbert was 15 of 21 for 131 yards and got sacked six times. He had his second rushing TD of the week, somersaulting into the end zone to cut Los Angeles' deficit to 17-10 at the end of the first half. The Chargers got help from embattled Jets coach Aaron Glenn when he took all three of his timeouts in the final two minutes of their drive.
The Jets chewed up 30 minutes on the clock in their five scoring drives.
Jets: At Miami next Sunday.

title: Lipscomb secures 92-67 win over Milligan
summary: Sawyer Dotson had 14 points in Lipscomb’s 92-67 victory over Milligan

title: Jonah Coleman powers Broncos past Raiders 38-24 as Denver honors the late Tom Jackson
summary: Jonah Coleman ran for 111 yards and three touchdowns and the Denver Broncos beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24
story: Jonah Coleman ran for 111 yards and three touchdowns and the Denver Broncos beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24

DENVER -- Forty years after his retirement from football and 48 hours after his death at age 75, the Denver Broncos set aside a game ball for Tom Jackson in the aftermath of their 38-24 win Sunday over the Las Vegas Raiders.

“I'd be remiss if we didn't start just by honoring Tom Jackson tonight,” Broncos coach Sean Payton said as he began his postgame news conference. “He got a game ball tonight, his family. He was part of the rich history, obviously. A tough loss for everyone.”

Rookie Jonah Coleman ran for a season-best 111 yards and three touchdowns and the Broncos beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 on a solemn Sunday in the Mile High City as they honored the “Orange Crush” and ESPN great following his death on Friday.

Jackson's death was announced Sunday by longtime on-air partner Chris Berman, just as some of the Broncos' early risers were starting to arrive at Empower Field for top overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza's first career road start.

For the coin flip, Broncos great Champ Bailey wore a No. 57 Jackson jersey following a moment of silence and a video tribute to the fiery cornerstone of the defense that led Denver to its first Super Bowl appearance in 1977.
Linebacker Alex Singleton wore a bright orange Jackson jersey after the game, too.

He said the team watched film of the old AFC West rivalry Friday and No. 57 showed up again and again on the highlight reels, which of course included the famous clip where he told John Madden, “It's all over, fat man!” as the Broncos began to tilt the balance of power in the Broncos-Raiders rivalry in the late 1970s.
“Just what he means to the organization, what he means to the football world,” Singleton said, “he was a special guy and hopefully we did him justice today.”

Indeed, Denver's defense sacked Mendoza five times, hit him another 10 times, broke up seven of his passes and intercepted him once — that came from nickel back Ja'Quan McMillian, who sealed the win with a 35-yard, one-handed pick-6 with 1:52 remaining and the Broncos (8-2) clinging to a seven-point lead.
“We want the defense to be like that again,” Singleton said of the Jackson-led unit. “Orange Crush, stop-everybody defense, come to Mile High and get embarrassed.”
Coleman scored on runs of 1, 4 and 7 yards, the latter two after the Raiders (4-7) had erased a 17-0 deficit.

“It’s hard to play in this offense,” said tight end Evan Engram, who caught six passes for 74 yards Sunday. “It’s hard to be a rookie. I mean, I was in Year 9 last year in this offense (for the first time), and it was it was a grind for me to learn it.”
The Broncos kept pace with Kansas City atop the AFC West by winning their sixth consecutive game since Payton took back the offensive play-calling duties.
Mendoza finished 18 of 37 for 267 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He was bothered not only by the pass rush but the crowd noise.

“Those fans are crazy loud,” Mendoza said. “Played in some loud environments in my college days, but college is nothing like the NFL and they were very loud. And there was some helmet miscommunication as well, so that was another challenge that prevented itself, but just happy to work through those challenges and I think it was a great experience.”
Bo Nix completed 19 of 35 passes for 225 yards with one TD and an interception on a Hail Mary as the first half ended.
“I think it should be like basketball where if you chuck it from half court it doesn't count,” Nix cracked.

Las Vegas erased the final remnants of a 17-0 deficit when Mendoza hit tight end Ian Thomas for a 19-yard touchdown in the third quarter. The score came after Nix was stuffed by Maxx Crosby and Folorunso Fatukasi on a fourth-and-1 sneak from the Denver 39.
“I don't regret the call,” Payton said.

Coming off their bye week, the healthy Broncos had their most productive first half of the season, jumping out to a 17-0 lead. Denver's special teams blocked two of AJ Cole's punts, helping the Broncos win the field-position game.

Ashton Jeanty, whose 46-yard run set up Matt Gay's chip-shot field goal, slipped past linebacker Que Robinson on a wheel route and reeled in Mendoza's deep pass for a 68-yard touchdown that cut Denver's lead to 17-10 at the half. Jeanty finished with 79 yards on 11 carries and added five receptions for 90 yards.

Even though Mendoza has been sacked 11 times in two games — the same number of times Kirk Cousins was sacked in nine games before his deadline trade to Minnesota — Payton said he sees a potential Raiders resurgence led by Mendoza.
“A much different Raiders team than we're used to seeing,” Payton said.

Raiders coach Klint Kubiak, whose father, Gary, led the Broncos to their last Super Bowl title, was asked if he could talk about his emotions of returning to Denver, where he also cut his teeth as a coach.
“Yeah I could, I don’t want to,” he replied. “I wanted to win this game today and we didn’t win, and so we got to go win next week.”

Raiders TE Brock Bowers was inactive with ankle and quadriceps injuries. DL Tim Keenan III (knee) and DT Adam Butler (concussion) left the game, and DT JJ Pegues appeared to injure his left shoulder in the waning minutes.
Broncos DE Sai'vion Jones left with 1:37 remaining with an unspecified injury.
Raiders: Visit the Cleveland Browns next Sunday.
Broncos: Visit the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday.

title: NFL defends incomplete pass ruling on Parker Washington's would-be TD in Jaguars' loss at Giants
summary: The NFL has defended a questionable call that Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Parker Washington did not catch the ball in the back of the end zone for what would have been a fourth-quarter touchdown
story: The NFL has defended a questionable call that Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Parker Washington did not catch the ball in the back of the end zone for what would have been a fourth-quarter touchdown

EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Parker Washington thought he caught the ball for a crucial touchdown in the fourth quarter, and Jacksonville Jaguars coach Liam Coen was confident enough that he challenged the initial call of an incomplete pass.
The NFL did not see it that way.
The league defended its decision after the Jaguars lost 23-18 at the New York Giants on Sunday, ruling that Washington did not complete the catch.

“It was determined that the receiver did not gain full control of the ball until he was out of bounds,” vice president of instant replay Mark Butterworth told a pool reporter. “He needs to maintain control of the ball throughout the process of the catch.”
Coen relayed that he was told “the ball switched hands.
“That was what it came down to,” Coen said.
Washington felt good about possession but also did not want to blame the defeat on the officiating.
“I saw it on the Jumbotron or whatever we call it,” Washington said. “It didn’t go our way. You can’t hang your head on that. We’ve got to move on and get ready for the next play.”
Trevor Lawrence, who threw two interceptions while under pressure for much of the game, similarly did not want to lament the impact of the would-be touchdown on the result.

“It’s a close play,” Lawrence said. “Obviously, they called it and said it wasn’t. It’s tough. I thought it was incredible that he gave us a shot there and he caught it, and it looked like he had two feet down, but it was close. You can’t leave in the refs’ hands. I think it’s a tough call for them.”
CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore, who was an official in the league for 15 years, disagreed with the decision.
“I still had the right foot down as he's falling,” Steratore said on the broadcast. “I see the ball move a little bit, but I did not think he lost possession of the football.”
Giants coach John Harbaugh was fine with it, saying he thought simply “the ball moved.”

story: Karl-Anthony Towns had 30 points and 13 rebounds, Jalen Brunson added 22 points, and the New York Knicks beat the Indiana Pacers 113-106 to extend their winning streak to five games

NEW YORK -- Karl-Anthony Towns had 30 points and 13 rebounds, Jalen Brunson added 22 points, and the New York Knicks beat the Indiana Pacers 113-106 on Sunday night to extend their winning streak to five games.
Towns, who missed Saturday night’s buzzer-beater victory over Portland due to an illness, shot 9 for 14 from the field including 4 for 4 on 3-pointers.

Landry Shamet scored 17 points while Josh Hart finished with 10 points, 11 assists and 10 rebounds for the Knicks. It was Hart's 18th triple-double with the Knicks, tying Michael Ray Richardson for second on the team’s career list. Walt Frazier holds the team record with 23.
The Knicks were without OG Anunoby, who missed his second straight game because of tightness in his left calf. Backup guard Deuce McBride was held out due to tightness in the left abductor.
Pascal Siakam scored 25 points, Andrew Nembhard finished with 16 and Ivica Zubac had 10 points and 14 rebounds for the Pacers, who have lost their last four games.
Towns in the closing minutes of the third quarter outscored Indiana 10-2, capping it off with a 3-pointer that extended the Knicks lead 86-74 with 54 seconds left in the period.
Indiana fell behind by 12 points after Mikal Bridges hit a 3-pointer that made it 92-80 and trimmed it to 95-87 following a three-point play from Kelly Oubre Jr. with 7:31 left in the fourth quarter.
A fadeaway jumper from Brunson increased the Knicks advantage to 110-95 — their largest lead of the night — with 2:35 remaining.
The Pacers kept it close and went on a 6-0 run capped by a layup from Obi Toppin that made it 112-106 with 25 seconds remaining.
Brunson then put the game out of reach with a free throw after Quenton Jackson was called for a foul away from the ball.

title: Faizon Brandon's 2 long TD runs in the fourth quarter lift No. 9 Tennessee past LSU, 27-13
summary: Faizon Brandon had two long touchdown runs in the fourth quarter and No. 9 Tennessee’s stifling defense proved critical in a 27-13 victory over LSU on Saturday
story: Faizon Brandon had two long touchdown runs in the fourth quarter and No. 9 Tennessee’s stifling defense proved critical in a 27-13 victory over LSU on Saturday

KNOXVILLE, Tenn. -- Faizon Brandon had two long touchdown runs in the fourth quarter, Tennessee's stifling defense shut down LSU late, and the No. 9 Volunteers beat the Tigers 27-13 on Saturday to maintain their place in the College Football Playoff hunt.

Brandon, a freshman who shared time at quarterback with George MacIntyre, broke a 13-all tie with an 18-yard touchdown run, then added a 55-yard scoring scamper with just over 4 minutes remaining to put the game away.
MacIntyre was just 12 of 21 for 79 yards with a touchdown pass.

The Vols (9-2, 6-2 SEC), who were ranked ninth in the latest poll released by the playoff selection committee, struggled on offense most of the game. They committed three turnovers, were 3 of 16 on third down and finished with 325 yards of total offense.
LSU (6-5, 3-5) couldn't handle the Vols' defense, though.

Sam Leavitt threw for 222 yards and a touchdown, but he also was sacked eight times. The Tigers ran 34 times for 43 yards, an average of just 1.3 per carry. And coach Lane Kiffin's team was flagged 16 times, eight of which were false starts, thanks in part to a raucous crowd packed inside of Neyland Stadium.

LSU's only touchdown, a pass from Leavitt to Tre'Dey Green in the third quarter, came only after the Vols' Qua Moss muffed a punt and the Tigers recovered on the Tennessee 9. It sent the game to the fourth quarter tied 13-all.

With 3:14 remaining, and the Vols leading by two touchdowns, a pass interference call on Moss led to fans tossing golf balls on the field. The game was stopped as LSU left its sideline and stood in the middle of the field to avoid direct hits.

Tennessee led 10-6 after a defensive first half in which the teams combined for just 235 yards. LSU got two field goals off Tennessee turnovers, while MacIntyre hit DaSaahn Brame with a 2-yard TD pass to give the Vols the lead at the break.
LSU: Kiffin is the first Tigers coach to lose five SEC games in his first season since Gaynell Tinsley in 1948.
Tennessee: The game was costly on the injury front for the Vols with linebacker Arion Carter leaving late with an ankle injury and running back DeSean Bishop with a leg injury.

summary: Cooper DiLeva kicked a 42-yard field goal as time expired as San Diego State scored nine points in the last two minutes to shock No. 15 Boise State 22-20
story: Cooper DiLeva kicked a 42-yard field goal as time expired as San Diego State scored nine points in the last two minutes to shock No. 15 Boise State 22-20
BOISE, Idaho -- Cooper DiLeva kicked a 42-yard field goal as time expired as San Diego State scored nine points in the last two minutes to shock No. 15 Boise State 22-20 on Saturday night.
Boise State (9-2, 6-1 Pac-12; No. 17 CFP) watched its playoff hopes take a big hit as the Broncos squandered a late 20-13 lead.
San Diego State (6-5, 5-2) clinched a spot in the Pac-12 championship game and will return to Boise for a rematch on Dec. 4.
Despite some early struggles, Boise State seemed poised to escape with a victory before the Aztecs rallied.

But a spectacular 37-yard touchdown catch by Jaylon Hawkins, in which he wrestled the ball away in the end zone from an apparent interception by Sherrod Smith, pulled San Diego State within 20-19 with 1:51 to play.
San Diego State couldn’t convert a 2-point conversion attempt and the Broncos recovered an onside kick, but couldn’t get a first down to salt away the game.
Instead of punting on fourth-and-3 at the Aztecs 45, Boise State coach Spencer Danielson went for the first down, but quarterback Maddux Madsen was dragged down for a 1-yard loss.
Stone Saunders, who threw for 227 yards and rushed for 41 more, only needed two completions of seven and 24 yards to set up DiLeva for the winning kick.
Madsen threw for 311 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions.

Boise State: After averaging more than 50 points in their last three games, the Broncos leaned on defense, which couldn’t deliver in the game’s biggest moments. The Boise State defense has been pushed to the brink in several games, and it finally cost them — not only the game but also possibly a playoff berth.

San Diego State: The Aztecs have played better defensively since melting down last month in a 56-49 loss to Colorado State. Now they have a chance to secure their first Pac-12 conference title in two weeks.

title: FIFA set to pick US-led bid as 2031 Women's World Cup host and UK project for 2035
summary: FIFA is preparing to confirm a United States-led bid to host the 2031 Women’s World Cup and a UK project led by England for the 2035 edition
story: FIFA is preparing to confirm a United States-led bid to host the 2031 Women’s World Cup and a UK project led by England for the 2035 edition
ZURICH -- A United States-led bid to host the 2031 Women’s World Cup and a UK project led by England for the 2035 edition are set to be confirmed Monday by FIFA.

FIFA has wanted those heavyweights of women’s soccer to face no opposition and lead hosting the first two tournaments of 48 teams and 104 games, bringing parity with the men’s World Cup. The 2027 Women's World Cup will have 32 teams in Brazil.
FIFA’s 211 member federations have been called to an online meeting hosted Monday from Zurich to confirm the pair of four-nation co-hosting candidates which never faced a rival bid.

The U.S. will host with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica in a project across the CONCACAF regional soccer body. The bid offers FIFA a choice from 20 cities: 14 in the U.S., four in Mexico plus San Jose in Costa Rica and Kingston, Jamaica.
The U.S. previously hosted the Women's World Cup alone in 1999 and 2003.
The United Kingdom bid teams England with Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales that offers a choice from 19 venues, including Wembley Stadium in London.
England never hosted a Women's World Cup which started with the 1991 tournament in China.

Northern Ireland is now included with Windsor Park in Belfast, with plans for a renovated 23,000-capacity stadium that is big enough for a Women’s World Cup but not for the men’s European Championship. Euro 2028 is being hosted by England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland, which has the 50,000-seat national soccer and rugby stadium in Dublin.
For the second time in less than two years, FIFA is confirming a double award of World Cup hosts without rival bids that gives clarity for the decade ahead.

In December 2024, FIFA member federations were asked to rubber-stamp the unprecedented six-nation, three-continent bid for the men’s World Cup in 2030 from Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay.
That cleared the way for FIFA to award also the 2034 World Cup to Saudi Arabia in a fast-track process that seemed designed to exclude other candidates.

title: Brown to Alexander duo leads Incarnate Word's offensive eruption in 66-3 win over East Texas A&M

story: Emmett Brown threw for 313 yards and four touchdowns and Incarnate Word overwhelmed East Texas A&M 66-3
COMMERCE, Texas -- Emmett Brown threw for 313 yards and four touchdowns, Patrick Batiste returned two interceptions for touchdowns, and Incarnate Word overwhelmed East Texas A&M 66-3 on Saturday.
Brown's 39-yard scoring pass to Roy Alexander early in the first quarter made it 7-0. Not longer after, Brown connected with Jamir Roberts for a 4-yard touchdown for a 14-0 lead.

His 44-yard scoring pass to Alexander with 8:55 left in the third made it 38-3. Alexander finished with 178 yards receiving on eight receptions.
David Rasor ran for 109 yard on just five carries which included a 40-yard touchdown run for the game's final score. Rasor's longest run of the game was 49 yards.

Defensively, the Cardinals (8-4, 7-2 Southland Conference) got a pair of pick-6s from Batiste, who intercepted Reese Mooney and ran it back 78 yards for a 45-3 lead. On East Texas A&M's next drive, in relief of Mooney, Nicky Johnson threw a pick to Batiste, who returned it 75 yards with 3:31 left in the third.
Johnson threw for 140 yards and Mooney had 129 passing for the Lions (3-9, 3-6).

East Texas A&M: Ends its season on a three-game losing streak.

title: Mercury gets its first visitor in years as a pair of spacecraft loop into orbit
summary: The European Space Agency announced BepiColombo's arrival via social media.
story: The European Space Agency announced BepiColombo's arrival via social media.

CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. -- A pair of spacecraft slipped into orbit around Mercury on Saturday after an eight-year cruise through the inner solar system to unravel our littlest planet's mountain of mysteries.

The linked robotic explorers — one European, the other Japanese — will separate from one another next month in order to map and study the scorching little planet from different altitudes. The $2 billion (1.7 billion euros) mission is known collectively as BepiColombo.

The European Space Agency announced BepiColombo's arrival via social media. A series of thruster firings slowed the spacecraft enough to be captured by the planet's weak gravity. But it took several anxious hours before flight controllers in Germany — 94 million miles (152 million kilometers) away — could confirm that BepiColombo had achieved orbit. Teams pored over the data streaming back; additional information was not immediately available.
BepiColombo is only the third spacecraft to visit Mercury — the sun's closest planet and barely bigger than our moon — and the first in more than a decade.

NASA's Mariner 10 flew past Mercury three times in the mid-1970s. The team included the late Italian mathematician Giuseppe “Bepi” Colombo, for whom this latest mission is named. NASA's Messenger spacecraft entered orbit around Mercury in 2011 and, after running out of fuel, crashed into the planet in 2015.

Launched in 2018, BepiColombo took a slower, more roundabout route to get to Mercury, flying once past Earth, twice past Venus and six times past Mercury for gravity-guiding assists. All those loop-de-loops put more than 6 billion miles (10 billion kilometers) on the odometer. The conjoined spacecraft shed their mother ship in September for the final leg of the journey.

Lead project scientist Geraint Jones said he and others can’t wait for all the new data to start streaming down in the spring. The mission will provide the ability to compare “unprecedented measurements taken by two spacecraft at the planet at the same time,” he noted.

Once orbiting separately, the European Space Agency's satellite and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency’s smaller craft will study Mercury’s dense interior and exterior magnetic field, as well as everything in between: impact craters, volcanic plains, mountain ridges and peaks jutting as high as 3 miles (4 1/2 kilometers).

The mercury at Mercury can hit more than 800 degrees (427 degrees Celsius), adding strain to electronic and engineering systems. Space agency officials want to keep the mission going for at least one Earth year — or the equivalent of four Mercury years.
“The spacecraft and its instruments need to be kept as cool as possible, which is a huge technical challenge in itself,” Jones said in an email.

Despite its relative proximity to Earth, Mercury is one of the solar system’s least explored planets. Only outer planets Uranus and Neptune have had fewer visitors — a lone Voyager 2 back in the 1980s.
