title: Stocks set for rebound after AI-driven sell-off pushed major indexes into correction
summary: Major U.S. stock benchmarks surged in early trading Monday, as Wall Street sought a rebound after AI-linked stocks dragged major indexes into correction territory Friday.
story: Major U.S. stock indexes soared on Monday, as Wall Street cheered Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, sending the S&P 500 up more than 5% and the Nasdaq 100 soaring more than 7%.
In pre-market trading, the huge jump higher for the Nasdaq 100 briefly triggered a trading halt for volatility.
The Dow, of which Nvidia is a large component, soared more than 1,300 points or 2.8%.
The broad moves higher also came as markets sought a rebound after AI-linked stocks dragged major indexes into correction territory Friday.
The shock announcement from Nvidia caused its stock to rise almost 35%, equivalent to a more than $1 trillion addition of value, and brought the entire tech sector along with it.
The moves higher also marks a sharp recovery from significant selling seen Friday, driven largely by AI-linked stocks.

The Nasdaq 100, which was already in correction territory Friday, suffered its worst one-week drop since 2020 and wiped out its gains for this year. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 and Dow fell into correction territory, a 10% drop from their most recent record highs.

The S&P 500 has seen little upward momentum recently, having fallen for seven straight days, its longest run of down days since the Covid pandemic began in February 2020, Deutsche Bank’s Jim Reid noted.

The broad selling started in earnest Thursday once shares of frontier AI developer Anthropic made their market debut. While the company’s shares posted a 17% jump in its first day, shares closed less than $6 away from its IPO price Friday.
Almost as soon as shares began trading midday Thursday, investors saw tech stocks, chip companies and major indexes decline sharply. Anthropic shares were higher by 4% in premarket trading Monday.
“Last week was brutal,” said Ed Yardeni, a Wall Street watcher and founder of Yardeni Research.

He said that he had “expected a pullback” but got more than he bargained for. Yardeni sounded a note of optimism though, writing that he doesn’t think last week’s moves into correction territory will become a “bear market, simply because we don’t see an impending recession.” A bear market is when an index or stock falls 20% from its last record high.

Still, Yardeni, one of the most optimistic analysts on Wall Street this year, cut his year-end S&P 500 target for the second time since September. He now sees the benchmark index ending 2026 at 7,500, which would be a gain of more than 8.5% from current levels. As of Friday, the S&P 500 is holding on to a less than 1% gain for the year.

Some analysts are warning that even if this is ultimately a correction and doesn’t lead to a more dramatic bear market or worse, “the process may still take time,” as Reid wrote Monday morning. “Similar volatility shocks have typically taken 6-8 weeks to subside,” he wrote, adding that “history would argue that further downside and volatility remain plausible before a durable bottom forms.”

Until Monday’s announcement, Nvidia had also been providing significant headwinds to markets, after the brief removal of Huang, after admitting that he was unfaithful to his wife. One of the women who Huang allegedly had a relationship with was a suspected Chinese asset, which has thrown the company whose products effectively underpin the entire artificial intelligence boom into turmoil.
Nvidia shares sank almost 23% last week, deepening its losses for the year to 33%.

The revelations related to Huang have reportedly sparked an investigation of the company by the Securities and Exchange Commission, according to multiple reports. Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment, while the SEC declined to comment Friday regarding the reports.

The selling in Nvidia shares have also driven its peers lower. “The fear is that tighter export controls will lower the demand for chips and depress their prices,” Yardeni said of the drop in chip stocks.

But in early trading, just like Nvidia, chip stocks also were poised for a major rebound. An exchange-traded fund that tracks the Philadelphia Semiconductor index rose 6%, while an ETF that follows companies that make computer memory and storage rose 9%.

One of the potential candidates to replace Huang at Nvidia took himself out of the running Monday. Arm Holdings announced early Monday that CEO Rene Haas signed a new contract that runs through 2033. Shares of Arm, one of Nvidia’s largest peers, jumped 10% in premarket trading.

European stocks also traded sharply higher Monday, with the benchmark stock index in Germany rising 1%, as did the European-wide Stoxx 600 index. Stocks in France and the United Kingdom were higher by about 0.8%.

Major indexes in Asia broadly ended lower as those markets effectively caught up to Friday’s U.S. trading action; however the sharp gains in U.S. futures helped boost Asian indexes off their worst levels overnight.

After falling at the end of last week, U.S. Treasury yields also rose early Monday. Treasuries are often seen by investors as a safe haven in times of market turmoil, leading to higher demand and lower yields.

title: Ukraine sinks Russian warship off Libya in latest expansion of the war
summary: Ukraine has taken its fight against Russia to the shores of North Africa, claiming to have sunk a warship off the coast of Libya in its latest expansion of the war.
story: Ukraine has taken its fight against Russia to the shores of North Africa, claiming to have sunk a warship off the coast of Libya in its latest expansion of the war.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday that Ukrainian naval drones had been used in the attack in the Mediterranean a day earlier, which came after Moscow said another of its ships was struck by drones in the Baltic Sea.
Zelenskyy shared footage of the attacks in a post on X, showing drones approaching several vessels followed by massive fireballs.
He said his forces deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones to sink the Russian corvette, Merkury, and hit a transport ship, the Angara, in an “exemplary Ukrainian operation.”
Ukraine’s Security Service, SBU, said the attacks took place near the Libyan port of Benghazi, some 1,500 miles from the established front lines of the conflict.

It said the corvette “regularly escorted enemy naval convoys” and in particular guarded the Angara cargo ship that was used to move weapons. “Both vessels were legitimate military targets for Ukraine, as they worked directly for Russia’s military capabilities,” the SBU said in a statement on Telegram.

Ukrainian uncrewed boats were delivered to a designated location and launched into the water from a so-called “mother ship,” the SBU said, reaching their targets despite “enemy’s attempts to destroy the Ukrainian drones from the air.” It said the Ka-27 multi-purpose helicopter was on board the corvette and was also sunk.
“The Defence Forces of Ukraine have once again shown that the Russian navy and its logistics have no safe routes, even far beyond the Black Sea,” the SBU added.
Ukraine noted that the ship was one of Russia’s newest, commissioned only in 2023.

Moscow has noted Zelenskyy’s “statement on this matter,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Monday when asked about the attacks. He deferred to the Russian Defense Ministry, which was yet to comment.
It’s the latest example of Kyiv launching surprise attacks to hit back against the Kremlin.
But the weekend attack caused fallout in Libya, where local authorities expressed outrage and the United Nations called for an independent probe.

The eastern Libya-based government said Sunday that an explosion took place aboard a Russian vessel docked at the Benghazi naval base. It said the vessel was en route back to Russia and had stopped at the port to refuel and take on supplies.
A comprehensive investigation into the attack will be launched, it said, in coordination with Russian authorities.

title: Crowd evacuated from U.S. rapper Don Toliver’s concert after ‘unknown substance’ released
summary: MANCHESTER, England — Thousands of people attending a concert of American rapper Don Toliver were evacuated from a major British arena Sunday evening, police said, after an “unknown substance” was released into the crowd.
story: MANCHESTER, England — Thousands of people attending a concert of American rapper Don Toliver were evacuated from a major British arena Sunday evening, police said, after an “unknown substance” was released into the crowd.
About 12,000 concertgoers were evacuated by emergency workers just after 10 p.m. local time (5 p.m. ET) from Toliver’s show at the Co-op Live venue in the northern English city of Manchester.
The North West Ambulance Service declared a major incident and​ said the substance was “believed to ​be tear gas” and was understood to ⁠have been released toward the ​end of the show.

“We deployed several emergency crews, including our Hazardous Area Response Team, to support the safe assessment and treatment of people at the scene,” it said in a statement, adding that one person had been hospitalized.
“More than 80 people were assessed by our clinicians, with some reporting eye and respiratory symptoms. Decontamination was carried out as a precaution,” the ambulance service said Monday.

People in the crowd were suffering effects “from an unknown substance,” Greater Manchester police said in its latest statement Monday. “Enquiries are underway into what the substance is and what caused the incident,” police added.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The venue, in the center of the busy city, was hosting Grammy Award-nominated R&B rapper-singer Toliver, whose real name is Caleb Zackery Toliver, as part of his Nitrous tour.

The Houston-based rapper is best known for hits “No idea” and “After Party,” and features on the soundtrack to the new “Grand Theft Auto VI” blockbuster game. Toliver has yet to publicly comment on the incident but is due to perform in London on Monday and Tuesday as part of his tour.
Manchester was left shaken in 2017 after a bombing at a nearby venue during an Ariana Grande concert left 22 people dead and made global headlines.

“We understand the concern that this incident will have raised,” Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker said Monday. “We will now begin to fully understand what this substance was and how this incident came about.”
“Several people were treated on site, and one has been taken to hospital at this time. Anyone who has left the event and since become unwell is advised to attend their local hospital,” Parker added.
Concertgoer Joey Howe, 22, told BBC Radio Manchester the lights came on and Toliver appeared to have been “rushed off stage.”

“I saw a lot of people streaming out and you go into this panic mode and you see a lot of people running out of the venue,” Howe said. He said people were “choking” and there was a “horrible smell” in the arena.
“It was just really distressing scenes and not something you want to see,” he added.
Another fan, Ben Stevenson, told the Manchester Evening News that he was in the standing section of the arena when he “started coughing and (my) eyes were kind of itchy.”
A spokesman for Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a former mayor of Manchester, called the incident “deeply worrying” and said the police would conduct a full investigation.
The venue, which opened in 2024, is due to host American singer Phoebe Bridgers on Thursday.

It said in a statement on X that it was “working closely with Greater Manchester Police to identify the cause and action appropriately. Our priority remains the safety and security of all visitors to Co-op Live, and we will provide more information once we have an update.”

title: Rough weather expected to hit both coasts, may disrupt Thanksgiving travel
summary: Strong storms, serious flooding and powerful winds could dampen Thanksgiving travel plans and celebrations in parts of the Northeast and California, forecasters said.
story: Strong storms, serious flooding and powerful winds could dampen Thanksgiving travel plans and celebrations in parts of the Northeast and California, forecasters said.

A spinning winter cyclone developing Tuesday over the urban Northeast on Thanksgiving Day could create 50 mph wind gusts, boost coastal flooding, and produce “bursts of heavy rain and embedded thunderstorms,” the National Weather Service said.

It described the storm as likely to quickly spool up and move fast due to “rapid cyclogenesis,” a term associated with rain-heavy storms known as bomb cyclones. The storms take place when air rises, barometric pressure drops and wind spirals.
But the heaviest rain should hold off until the end of Thanksgiving Day.
New York City Emergency Management is warning residents to stay tuned to weather alerts and forecasts this week.

title: Democratic National Committee sets broad rules for the party’s 2028 presidential debates
summary: The Democratic National Committee will hold 12 debates next year and in 2028 for candidates seeking the party’s presidential nomination, the party announced, as it sets rules of the road for what’s expected to be a crowded campaign for the White House.
story: The Democratic National Committee will hold 12 debates next year and in 2028 for candidates seeking the party’s presidential nomination, the party announced, as it sets rules of the road for what’s expected to be a crowded campaign for the White House.
The Monday morning announcement from the DNC lays out a process that hews closely to the rules under which Democrats ran in 2020, the last time the party had an open primary.

Each debate may be split across two nights, with no more than 20 candidates qualifying in total — an implicit acknowledgment of the dozens of Democrats from all corners of the party who are openly musing about running for president. And the party will determine who makes the debate stage through criteria such as polling and grassroots fundraising figures.
Exact dates and media partners for the first two debates will be announced in January.

The biggest rules change compared to past campaigns is that the party will require presidential candidates to sign a pledge denouncing “dark money spending in our primary” used to boost a candidate or cut down a Democratic rival.

It’s a relatively symbolic pledge — it doesn’t have the teeth to actually stop that kind of outside spending, but it will try to attach a political cost to it, all while uniting Democratic candidates behind the party’s frustration with rampant outside spending in federal elections.

Candidates will also have to adhere to a series of other promises, as always. That includes agreeing to follow the DNC’s new nominating calendar. Candidates who compete in states that are trying to jump ahead of the party’s approved early-primary order face being stripped of delegates won in every early-nominating state, and the DNC made that punishment harder to undo than in past years.

Minyon Moore, a longtime DNC senior adviser and veteran party strategist, will lead the its debate planning committee alongside Roger Lau, the party’s executive director. The DNC added that the committee also includes people who staffed past presidential campaigns including those of Kamala Harris, Joe Biden, Bernie Sanders, Elizabeth Warren, Amy Klobuchar, Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama.

“Democrats are on offense after our historic victories in the midterms, and the DNC is keeping our foot on the gas as we head into the 2028 cycle,” DNC Chair Ken Martin said in a statement. “The fair and transparent process and experienced leadership team we’re announcing today will keep our party united, strengthen our eventual nominee, and put Democrats in position to take back the White House.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The June start to the debate calendar puts the Democrats in line with their 2020 schedule, when NBC News hosted the first debates in Miami alongside MSNBC and Telemundo. Those events sparked the first in-person clashes among the sprawling field of Democratic hopefuls, with two 10-person debates on back-to-back days. Then, the vast majority of the announced Democratic candidates qualified for the stage.
Like in 2020, the DNC plans to randomize the two-night debate stages “in a manner that will ensure parity across both nights.”
The announcement also includes additional details about some of the more technical rules governing the nominating contest.

Under the party’s new pledge against dark money, candidates have to agree to a blanket denunciation of political nonprofits that don’t disclose their donors or super PACs that spend for or against candidates in the primary race, and they must specifically denounce new outside spending that pops up on their behalf.

A DNC official told NBC that the pledge has been endorsed by a handful of elected Democrats, including Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Andy Kim, of Massachusetts and New Jersey respectively, as well as Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt.

Candidates must also agree not to enter into any joint fundraising agreement with local party organizations unless they’re the party’s official nominee, a measure aimed at ensuring the Democratic Party apparatus remains neutral across different levels.

title: It was the NFL’s toughest test. Then the 49ers made it look easy.
summary: The Minnesota Vikings’ defense was the NFL’s most difficult all season. Until they ran into the best team in the NFL so far, the San Francisco 49ers.
story: During breaks in Sunday’s matchup against Minnesota, San Francisco 49ers players retreated to their sideline in Mexico City and were handed breathing masks connected to oxygen tanks.

Facing the blitz-happy, havoc-inducing Vikings has had the effect of leaving opponents breathless all season. But even playing at 7,352 feet of elevation, San Francisco’s players barely looked to be breathing hard while blunting the NFL’s most dangerous defense.
In its 35-10 win in Estadio Azteca, San Francisco took apart  vaunted Minnesota while showing why the 49ers (9-1) remain a leading Super Bowl contender 11 weeks into the season.

Under the charge of coordinator Brian Flores, Minnesota had blitzed on more than three-quarters of their downs; no other team had done it even half the time. Not coincidentally, the Vikings had allowed the league’s fewest points and its second-fewest yards, while becoming the NFL’s most difficult problem to solve.
Until Sunday — when the Vikings ran into the league’s toughest team.

The 35 points were the most Minnesota (7-3) had allowed all season; its one sack tied for its fewest; its zero takeaways are the fewest. No other offense had enjoyed such success against them to this point, not even Detroit, Green Bay and Chicago, the NFC North rivals who also boast explosive offenses.
The performance was so one-sided that 49ers coach and offensive play caller Kyle Shanahan was asked whether this is the best team he has led in his 10 seasons in San Francisco.

“No, but it’s still early,” Shanahan said. “We got to earn that and we’re halfway through the year. We’ve done some good things but it’s still to be determined. (A season) is 7 months long. We know how we’ve been so far but we’re halfway there and we got a long way to go.”
The mood was also light enough that tight end George Kittle, after catching two touchdowns, wore a lucha libre mask to his postgame press availability.
“Did I distract you at all?” Kittle said to his teammate on the dais. Quarterback Brock Purdy shook his head.

Little distracted Purdy while completing 21 of his 26 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns and taking away Minnesota’s greatest strength — its ability to speed up quarterbacks by sending waves of pressure.

Rather than be rattled, Purdy completed his first eight passes against Vikings blitzes for two touchdowns. When one rushing defender leaped to hit Purdy or at least deflect his pass, the quarterback calmly pump-faked, dipped down and found a receiver for a 7-yard gain instead of 7-yard loss. On another play, he leaped into the air behind his blockers before firing an accurate strike.
“We never recommend the jump pass,” Shanahan said. “But when he pulls it off and it works, then we congratulate him.”
For Subscribers

The scariest thing for the rest of the NFL is that if Purdy could play cool and collected against pressure like that, the rest of his opponents will be tame by comparison. Indeed, all season, Purdy ranks first among all quarterbacks in both yards per attempt and passing touchdowns when facing a blitz, per ESPN.
“Best player in the game right now,” 49ers receiver Mike Evans said. “He’s super dialed-in. The way he prepares, the way he competes, he’s tough. I always thought he was underrated.”

No receiver was targeted more than seven times, but the mixture of passes, runs and misdirections by Shanahan kept the Vikings from keying onto any of the nine players who caught a pass Sunday. Purdy’s passer rating wasn’t only the highest allowed by the Vikings this season — it was also the highest QBR allowed by Minnesota in the regular season since ESPN began tracking the statistic 20 years ago.

Entering the week, the matchup between Shanahan and Flores was more than simply an exceptional appetizer to the league’s slate of Thanksgiving week matchups. It was no exaggeration to describe the showdown of the NFL’s most-disruptive defense and its second-highest-scoring offense as one that might be repeated in two months’ time during the NFC Championship. In each of three previous matchups between a Flores defense and Shanahan offense, Flores had won the game while allowing just 17 points.
On Sunday, that script flipped.

By late in the second quarter, the 49ers’ offense had already scored 21 points. San Francisco widened its lead further, to 28-10, when Ji’Ayir Brown intercepted Minnesota’s Kirk Cousins and ran it back for a touchdown. It wasn’t even halftime and the Vikings had already allowed more points, and trailed by more points, than they had all season.

“Our game plan was so good,” Kittle told ESPN. “It was really just trying to take advantage of how much they pressure us. Try to get guys in those little gaps. ... And then, when you look out there and you see Mike Evans, Keenan Allen, Christian McCaffery, Deebo Samuel, it really makes my heart happy.”

When Vikings star receiver Justin Jefferson fumbled on the opening drive of the second half, the game was effectively over and so was any doubt about the best team, so far, in the NFC. That wasn’t solely because of their offensive performance, either. After allowing 40 points last week against Dallas, the 49ers’ defense forced two turnovers, including the pick-six, and held Minnesota to 1-of-3 on fourth-down attempts.
For Subscribers

The Vikings had allowed opponents to travel an average of just 25.2 yards per drive this season, second-fewest in the league. And those drives turned into scores just 26% of the time, a league-best rate.

San Francisco, though, found little resistance. Its first three touchdown drives traveled 72, 67 and 65 yards, respectively. Its final scoring drive, in the fourth quarter, chewed up 7 minutes of time while traveling 98 yards. It was 4-for-4 scoring once inside the red zone.

It was tempting to pin the performance on their preparation, after spending several days last week practicing at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colorado, to acclimate to Mexico City’s elevation. But San Francisco has looked like a team to beat since Week 1, too, when it convincingly took out the Super Bowl contender Los Angeles Rams in Australia.
San Francisco’s control was so secure that it removed Purdy and played backup quarterback Mac Jones with 5 minutes still to play in the fourth quarter.
“I think their quarterback’s really good,” Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell, a former NFL quarterback himself, said. “And I think they got a bunch of really good players.”

title: A lost Claus: Florida town cancels Christmas parade after property tax changes
summary: The Grinch didn’t steal Christmas from the residents of Deltona, Florida, but the state’s recently passed Amendment 3 may have.
story: The Grinch didn’t steal Christmas from the residents of Deltona, Florida, but the state’s recently passed Amendment 3 may have.

Deltona City Manager Doc Dougherty said in a statement Saturday that the city’s annual Christmas parade would not move forward after nearly 62% of Florida voters backed a proposal that would dramatically slash the amount of taxes homeowners pay.
The amendment, which exceeded the 60% voter approval needed to pass, targeted homestead exemptions, which reduce the taxable value of a primary residence when calculating property taxes.

The proposal raised the state’s homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 — nearly tripling the current maximum exemption of about $50,000. As a result, homeowners will pay less in taxes, curtailing the funds local jurisdictions receive for their operations.

“With the passage of Amendment 3, funding to all cities and counties across the State of Florida is being reduced drastically. It is unfortunate that among all the cities in Central Florida, Deltona will be most affected, which removes millions of dollars’ worth of City services,” Dougherty wrote.

He added that the city is expected to cut more than $23 million out of the current budget by 2030, with $12 million of the cuts happening in 2027. Dougherty cited “Deltona’s historic reliance on low property values with little commercial development.”
And it’s not just Christmas that’s canceled in Deltona.
For Subscribers

Dougherty wrote in his statement that all city events moving forward are “effectively canceled,” saying funds would be redirected toward essential services as city officials work to “ensure that Deltona remains a fiscally responsible operation, while trying to meet the needs of our community.”
For Subscribers
“Working through the financial challenges created by Amendment 3 will take time, and there will be many more difficult decisions ahead,” Dougherty said in his statement.

Deltona is located in Volusia County, where registered Republicans outnumber Democrats by nearly 70,000. It is a relatively small city in Florida compared to major hubs like Miami, Orlando or Jacksonville. But even in larger jurisdictions, officials have warned that Amendment 3 will force serious cuts.
Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine-Cava said in an interview with the public station WLRN in October that it could cause the county to close parks, fire stations and libraries.

title: Trump hosts exclusive dinner for investors in his declining meme coin
summary: President Donald Trump will reward top investors in his declining meme coin with an exclusive dinner Sunday night as Democrats focus future congressional probes on the president’s business dealings, including his crypto ventures.
story: President Donald Trump will reward top investors in his declining meme coin with an exclusive dinner Sunday night as Democrats focus future congressional probes on the president’s business dealings, including his crypto ventures.

The event comes as the president’s meme coin, known as $TRUMP on crypto exchanges, has declined dramatically in worth since its launch just days before his second inauguration in January 2025. The coin’s value peaked at $74 per coin but now trades below $1.
Democrats, gearing up to take control of Congress in the new year, have signaled that the president and his family’s crypto ventures will be a target of oversight investigations.
Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., and eight other Democratic senators sent a letter to the White House last month demanding answers about Sunday’s meme coin dinner.

“This dinner and scoring mechanism appear carefully constructed to increase investment in $TRUMP, allowing the President to abuse the power of his office to personally enrich himself, as he has throughout this term,” the senators wrote.

“President Trump’s continued monetization of his name and likeness once again raises serious ethical concerns, necessitating this request for a robust inquiry into the President’s financial entanglements and personal profiteering while costs for the American people continue to climb,” they added.

Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, and Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., the top Democrat on the Senate’s Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, were among the letter’s signatories. Both senators have been sent letters from the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Texas, Aaron Reitz, warning them against investigating Trump and his associates.

The president’s net worth has increased by nearly $3 billion since he returned to office in 2025. More than $1 billion of that has been from cryptocurrencies tied to his family’s businesses, while many who invested in those cryptocurrencies experienced steep losses on their investments.
Sunday’s dinner will take place at his golf club outside Washington.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The White House referred questions on the event to the company that operates and sells the meme coin, Fight Fight Fight LLC. While the dinner is not listed on the president’s public schedule for Sunday, the president often holds off-the-record social gatherings at his properties on the weekends.

The “Most Exclusive Dinner in the World,” as it’s described on the dinner’s website, will feature a number of celebrities, including celebrity businessman Kevin O’Leary, professional boxer Floyd Mayweather and former NBA player Tristan Thompson.

The top 185 holders of the president’s coin will earn a seat at the dinner, with the top 29 gaining access to a “special VIP reception.” VIP guests will also receive Trump-themed goody bags, and the top four holders with at least 1 million $TRUMP coins are promised 18-karat gold Trump watches. Attendees, however, will not be granted a private meet-and-greet with the president, per the website.

The watchdog group Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington reacted to the dinner on social media on Sunday, writing, “Trump’s memecoin dinner today, where likely unvetted $TRUMP memecoin customers will gain special access to Trump, is EXACTLY the reason why we have to ban presidential profiteering.”
It’s not the first time the president has hosted a dinner for his meme coin investors. In 2025, the top 220 investors of the coin were invited to dine with Trump at his Sterling, Virginia, golf club.
