The performance comes over a decade after she last took the stage at the awards show with Vince Gill and Alison Krauss, singing “Red.” At that 2013 ceremony, Swift was also given the Pinnacle Award, a rare accolade that is given to artists who have “undeniably redefined the pinnacle of success in the genre.” It was presented to her by artists she had previously opened for, including Tim McGraw, Faith Hill and George Strait.

After a quick outfit change, Swift returned to the stage later on to present the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award, an accolade given to the artist who “has attained the highest degree of recognition in Country Music.” Dynamic duo Brooks & Dunn ended up taking home the honor.

Earlier in the night, Swift, a two-time CMA Entertainer of the Year, was also among the nominees for single of the year for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” the singer’s 26th CMA nomination.  Ella Langley ended up winning the accolade with her hit song “Choosin’ Texas.”

But before the ceremony even began, Swift had already made waves across social media for her red carpet look. The singer arrived in a striking yellow strapless gown with a bubble hem from fashion house Oscar de la Renta. She finished the look with gold metallic heels and a classic updo.
“Petition for Taylor to wear yellow more often because she literally looks like a ray of sunshine,” one fan wrote on platform X.
Fans have been awaiting her return to the ceremony after the singer in September wrote in her Instagram stories that she hadn’t “YEED MY LAST HAW” in response to her nomination.

title: See TODAY’s First Weather Forecast Hand-Drawn by Host Dave Garroway in 1952
summary: Original TODAY host Dave Garroway did the first forecast on the show during its first episode on Jan. 14, 1952.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at the very first forecast during the show’s debut broadcast on Jan. 14, 1952.
Before there was Willard Scott or Al Roker, there was Dave Garroway. The original TODAY host was also the first person to do the weather on the show during its premiere episode on Jan. 14, 1952.
While the forecast is one of TODAY’s staples, the first one was a little bit off-kilter, complete with primitive technology that made it a challenge for Garroway. It also shows how far we’ve come.
How Did Dave Garroway Do the Weather?
Garroway was in the studio, chatting on a phone with Jim Fidler, who he said was “with the weather bureau.”
Garroway erased a chalkboard map of the United States while letting viewers in on how Fidler, who was based in Washington, D.C., is helping.

“Jim is our official U.S. weather forecaster, you understand, right  in the weather bureau where they make the stuff,” Garroway said as he readied himself to get Fidler’s information and began to write on the map before technical issues surfaced.
“I can’t hear you on the studio PA,” Garroway said while he fumbled with the phone.
A booming voice from overhead then indicated he’d have to get the information over the phone instead of the PA system, allowing Garroway to repeat what Fidler was saying.
Garroway then wrote out the various forecasts around the country in chalk on the map.
“I want you to know your forecast is very good because it’s raining right here in New York,” Garroway said to Fidler before he carried on writing on the chalkboard, courtesy of his colleague’s notes.
Who Was Jim Fidler?
Fidler, who died in 2007, played a large part in the first forecast, even if viewers couldn’t see or hear him.
He had a deep background in meteorology and radio and his work with TODAY netted NBC the outstanding service award to meteorology from a corporation from the American Meteorological Society in 1953.
That award was given out to the network “for performing an important public service through television coverage of the weather on its network programs,” according to the AMS.
What Did Dave Garroway Say About Doing the Forecast?
At the end of his forecast, Garroway explained how they would normally hear Fidler’s voice over the studio PA.
“Usually, you’ll be able to hear Jimmy’s voice,” he said. “The line to Washington has been a little busy this morning. It didn’t come quite through on time.”
Garroway also assured viewers that mistakes were bound to happen with a new program like TODAY.
“There’ll be lots of bugs on this show, by the way, from time to time. This is a fairly ambitious undertaking. Just expect a few bugs,” he said.

“Like somebody said: We’re like a play in New Haven for the first week. We’re getting ready to come into the big town. Well, we’ll be like that for a while, but don’t mind it ‘cause we don’t mind it.”

title: Pierce Brosnan Congratulates Robert Pattinson on Being Cast As James Bond: ‘You Are Going To Be Magnificent’
summary: Pierce Brosnan, who portrayed James Bond across seven years and four films, welcomed Robert Pattinson into “the world of Bond” in a sweet Instagram post on Nov. 18.
story: Robert Pattinson has received a blessing from 007 himself.

Pierce Brosnan, who portrayed James Bond across seven years and four films, welcomed Pattinson into “the world of Bond” in a sweet Instagram post on Nov. 18. It comes just two days after it was announced that Pattinson would step into the role of the famous British secret agent for the upcoming film.
“Dear Robert, Welcome to the world of Bond,” Brosnan wrote in the post. “You are going to be magnificent.”
Pattinson will portray 007 in the film, which will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, the brains behind the “Dune” trilogy. He will be the seventh person to take on the iconic role.
Brosnan, who portrayed the agent from 1995 to 2002, starred in franchise films “GoldenEye,” “Tomorrow Never Dies,” “The World Is Not Enough” and “Die Another Day.”

In his message to Pattinson, Brosnan reminisced on their shared experience, making the 2010 romantic drama “Remember Me.” Pattinson had portrayed main character Tyler Hawkins while Brosnan played his father Charles Hawkins.
“I have fond memories of our time together making ‘Remember Me,’” Brosnan wrote. “It has been a joy to watch you create a remarkable body of work and to go from strength to strength.”
Brosnan concluded the warm message with a sweet word of advice.
“Enjoy the ride,” Brosnan wrote before signing off with the Gaelic term for “lots of love.” “Grá mor, Pierce”

Fans couldn’t help but chime in on the post, calling for Brosnan’s involvement in the upcoming Bond film. Some demanded Brosnan return as a villain, while others recommended he be cast in the role of M, the mysterious head of the British Secret Intelligence Service.
Whaddya say, Pierce?

title: Lainey Wilson, Vince Gill Open the CMA Awards With a Powerful Dolly Parton Tribute
summary: The Queen of Country just got a royal tribute at the Country Music Awards.
story: The Queen of Country just got a royal tribute at the Country Music Awards.

The ceremony, which kicked off in Nashville, Tennessee Nov. 18, opened with an emotional performance by Lainey Wilson and Vince Gill, singing the Parton’s smash hit “I Will Always Love You in a dazzling homage to Dolly Parton. The late singer, a trailblazing force in the country music genre, died in August after a brief battle with cancer.
“Now our Tennessee angel is with the angels,” Wilson said before the performance. “Dolly, thank you for all you meant to us, and we will always love you.”
In the tribute, Gill and Wilson brought the crowd to their feet with their rendition of the ballad.
As the camera panned across the audience, several big stars including Luke Combs and Taylor Swift were seen getting emotional during the tribute.

Parton, whose country career spanned nearly 60 years, was a mainstay in both the genre and at the awards ceremony. Earning well over three dozen nominations, the “Jolene” singer took home 10 CMA awards, including the CMA’s Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award in 2016

The Country Music Association, the organization behind the awards ceremony, previously held a two-hour celebration of the star’s legacy in October. The memorial featured a star-studded lineup of performances from Little Big Town to Kelsey Ballerini.

“At the end of the day, few artists define Country Music better than the one-word, Dolly. Over her decades-long career, I worked with her on a number of programs,” Sarah Trahern, CEO of the Country Music Association said in a press release. “She was always the most professional in every setting, often walking off the bus in heels and hair and makeup ready to go, before expected and before the cast and crew.”
Trahern added that in addition to Parton’s music, the community’s “biggest loss” is “her work as a philanthropist and the genuine difference she has made in people’s lives throughout the world.”
“There will only ever be one Dolly,” Trahern said.

title: Taylor Swift Lights Up CMA Awards Red Carpet With Striking Yellow Gown
summary: Taylor Swift arrived at the Country Music Association Awards in Nashville, Tennessee on Nov. 18 and immediately turned the red carpet into a fashion show, strutting her stuff in a striking yellow gown.
story: Taylor Swift may be associated with “Red,” but she can absolutely rock the color yellow.
Swift arrived at the Country Music Association Awards in Nashville, Tennessee on Nov. 18 and immediately turned the red carpet into a fashion show. She strutted her stuff in a striking yellow gown.
And while she’s scheduled to perform at the event, she doesn’t even need to do so to impress the internet.
Social media feeds quickly filled with comments from fans, declaring the singer a “goddess” and “queen.”
Swift’s ensemble features a high-low strapless dress from Oscar de la Renta’s Spring 2027 collection, paired with metallic gold heels. She finished the look with a classic updo and dangling earrings.
The “Patient Zero” singer’s return to the scheduled return to the stage marks her first performance at the ceremony in 13 years.
Swift is also nominated for single of the year for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” the singer’s 26th CMA award nomination.

title: Florence Pugh Calls Out Scrutiny of Her Appearance and Opens Up About Health Journey: ‘Happy and Truly Respecting My Body’
summary: Florence Pugh has a strong message for anyone who feels entitled to make unwelcome comments about her appearance.
story: Florence Pugh has a strong message for anyone who feels entitled to make unwelcome comments about her appearance.

On Nov. 18, the actor shared a lengthy statement on social media in response to rumors that she may have had plastic surgery or taken weight-loss medication. Pugh also shared a powerful message about her ongoing journey towards self-acceptance.
In the statement, the actor wrote that she “turned 30 and my New Year’s resolution was to change my relationship with alcohol, and to be able to do at least one pull up in the gym.”

“It’s funny to see you all use reference images from times where I was really mentally unhappy and abusing my body and put it next to the image from the governors awards the other night where I am happy and truly respecting my body,” Pugh said, referencing the chatter around her look at the Nov. 15 awards ceremony in Hollywood.
Pugh added that she has “f------ worked so hard to clean my head and clean my body because I don’t want to allow space for negativity in my mind to grow.”
“I’m looking after myself, and that’s literally it,” she wrote.

Pugh was seemingly referring to the content of a Nov. 17 Instagram Reel from Evie magazine on which she left a comment. In the reel, the magazine suggested that Pugh had “fallen victim to Hollywood’s war on round faces.”

“A lot of people are pointing out how Florence used to have full, beautiful cheeks that made her face super recognizable. Now that her jaw is more defined, her chin is more pointier, her jaws are more sharp, it makes sense why people are wondering if she’s had work done,” says Nikki Yabut, the Evie magazine content creator in the video.
Pugh commented on the post, slamming the discussion around her appearance.

“Guys. I turned 30. I’m a woman. Body’s and faces change,” Pugh wrote. “It’s not that deep, the fact that people can’t even tell between what’s aging and what’s surgery is disturbing. Sadly puppy fluff doesn’t last forever ❤️.”
In a statement provided to TODAY.com, Yabut said in part that she “never claimed” that Pugh had plastic surgery, “nor do I condone the harsh comments about her appearance.”

“I’ve always thought Florence was and is beautiful, and I admire her personality as well and how she uses her platform,” Yabut said in the statement, adding that she had intended to call out Hollywood’s normalizing of cosmetic procedures.

In her new Instagram post, Pugh referenced the widespread discussion of her appearance, saying that she finds it “so stressful” to wake up to “thousands of people talking about you and your body in ways that you can’t even comprehend.”

“I’m aware that the culture on socials currently is very interested in talking about people’s surgery and ozempic changes, it’s clearly a part of our time right now, that there’s this frenzy of people picking apart what’s truth and what’s fake,” she wrote.
She added that “quite a lot of you” were discussing her appearance in “such a disturbing way.”
“I learnt online that I had been on Ozempic?” she wrote. “I learnt that I’d had upper bleph? Lower bleph? Filler? Face lipo? Buc[c]al fat remover? Chin surgery? Nose surgery?!”
Pugh then questioned how “one person COULD get all of these things done over night.”

The 30-year-old noted that she’s spent her entire career  “defending and protecting bodies that just grow the way they grow” and said she was “subjected to fat shaming in the business”  since the beginning of her career.

Pugh also addressed the rumors head-on, saying she has never had face surgery and has never been on Ozempic. She went on to explain how any changes in her appearance are simply related to lifestyle changes she’s put into practice.
The actor wrote that she’s prioritized adding muscle this year, and can now do six pull ups and lift 110 kilograms.
Pugh pointed out how she has received “daily” comments about her body ever since she’s been in the public eye and encouraged people to be more sensitive.

“Let’s use this as a moment of self reflection. If you were one of those people that have the instinct to pull apart bodies, I think let’s start with asking yourself why? And what you get from it? And it’s ok to admit to yourself that it comes from something deeper. I’m not angry at you, I’m angry at the situation that’s being projected on to us,” she wrote.
“It feels inescapable, but part of changing the tide is on you as much as us in the public eye, she continued.

title: Christina Ricci Reveals Cher Is Holding a Nearly 30-Year ‘Grudge’ Against Her Over a Voicemail
summary: Christina Ricci says Cher has held a grudge for decades over an unreturned voicemail. The “Mermaids” star explained the rift on “Watch What Happens Live.”
story: Christina Ricci says she and Cher, her co-star in the 1990 film “Mermaids,” haven’t spoken in years due to a rift that started when Ricci was 19.

Ricci, 46, who played Cher’s younger daughter in the film when she was 9, told the story on the Nov. 17 episode of “Watch What Happens Live With Andy Cohen,” Bravo’s late-night talk show. Cohen asked whether she was still in touch with Cher, who is 80.
“I’m not,” she said. “Unfortunately, she’s still mad at me. She holds a grudge.”

The trouble began when a magazine interviewed Cher for a profile of the young actor. Ricci wasn’t sure whether it was Rolling Stone or Premiere, but she remembered Cher’s comments in it as “not that amazing about me,” she said.
Then came the phone call.
“She left me a voicemail about how journalists are always trying to get the worst things,” Ricci recalled, “and she was so sorry.
“And I was 19, and so I didn’t return that message,” she added.
Cohen asked if that was why Cher was upset. “I’m pretty sure,” Ricci said. She added that she tried to get in touch with Cher since then and hasn’t heard back.
Nearly three decades on, Ricci said she still “adores” Cher and has had time to think about it from the other end of the line.

“I absolutely, 100%, can imagine being Cher and being like, ‘Oh my God, they misquoted me, and I’m going to call this young person and explain to her,’” she said. “And then the gall of that young person to not return the call. I would be so pissed. I get it.”
TODAY.com has reached out to a representative for Cher for comment.

“Mermaids,” directed by Richard Benjamin, starred Cher as Rachel Flax, a restless single mother in the early 1960s who keeps moving her two daughters from town to town. Winona Ryder played the older daughter, Charlotte.
It was one of Ricci’s first film roles. She went on to star in “The Addams Family,” “Casper,” “The Ice Storm” and more recently, the Showtime drama “Yellowjackets.”
Before the segment ended, Ricci turned to the camera.
“Love you, Cher,” she said. “I love you so much.”

title: Druski Manifested His Comedy Success in a 2018 Tweet. He Reveals His Next Big Goal on TODAY
summary: Druski tweeted in 2018 his goal to be one of the biggest comedians in the world. Eight years later, he reveals his next lofty goal on TODAY.
story: Druski spoke his success into existence.

Before he landed a Netflix deal and before he became the youngest person to host the BET Awards and the first content creator to host “Saturday Night Live,” the 32-year-old posted a tweet back in 2018 about his ambitions.
“I will be 1 of the Biggest Comedians in the World .......,” he said.
The comedian, whose real name is Drew Desbordes, spoke to Craig Melvin, Al Roker and Dylan Dreyer on TODAY Nov. 18 about what prompted him to post that tweet.

“I’m big on manifesting,” he said. “I’ve always been one of those big believers that I write things down, and they come true. In that moment, I was very serious about that, and I was adamant, and I made it happen, so I’m grateful.”

Druski is coming off an “SNL” appearance that gave the show its highest rating in two years. His latest achievement is the upcoming release of his first Netflix special, a semi-scripted comedy series called “Collect & Praise” that drops on Dec. 1. Druski plays a money-hungry megachurch pastor with comedian Mike Epps as his scheming deacon in a series that Druski said was shot in less than two weeks.
He’s also appearing in his first movie role in 2027 in “The Catch,” an upcoming baseball romantic comedy starring Oscar winner Emma Stone and directed by Stone’s husband, Dave McCary.

“It was the first time in a long time I felt like a student again,” Druski said. “Being around just great actors and how good they are, watching how prepare and the small things they do, I’m just trying to learn.”
The experience also has him ready to manifest another lofty goal by speaking it out loud.
“Oh man, Oscar,” he said. “I got to get that Oscar! It’s on the way.”
He made the TODAY hosts echo his sentiment to help put it out into the universe. Al went a step further and said Druski is on his way to the coveted Oscar, Grammy, Tony and Emmy award superfecta.
“Druski, Oscar,” Al said. “Beginning of the EGOT.”
“Now we talking,” Druski said.

title: I Study James Bond for a Living. Here’s How I Reacted to the Robert Pattinson Casting (and Who I Would’ve Picked)
summary: What do James Bond experts think of Robert Pattinson’s casting?
story: “Take it From Me” is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this, James Bond scholars weigh in on Robert Pattinson’s casting.
James Bond fans who waited seven long years to find out which actor would be the next to play the iconic British spy have gotten their answer.
Pattinson, Robert Pattinson.
Amazon MGM, which owns the rights to the Bond films, announced the choice on Nov. 16, which predictably left longtime fans either shaken or stirred.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos revealed that he was involved in the decision at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event in California. “We ran a really tight process and we made the final decision on Friday,” Bezos said, per NBC News reporting.

He added that there was a “big group” of actors who did “real, old-fashioned screen tests” to compete for the role. “There was something special about Rob and his performances,” Bezos said. “It was immediately un-debated. We all gravitated toward Rob.”

The 40-year-old star of “The Batman” and “The Odyssey” will succeed Daniel Craig, whose last Bond film was released in 2021. If the next Bond film is not released until 2028, it will have been the longest hiatus between movies in the franchise’s 64-year history, so the fans are thirsty for a new version.
TODAY.com discussed the casting choice with a trio of Bond scholars:

Oliver Buckton, the author of the Ian Fleming biography “The World Is Not Enough” and a professor and chair of the Department of English at Florida Atlantic UniversityColin Burnett, program director of Film & Media Studies at Washington University in St. Louis, and author of the forthcoming book “James Bond and the Art of Franchise Storytelling”James Chapman, the author of “Licence to Thrill: A Cultural History of the James Bond Films.”
Oliver Buckton, the author of the Ian Fleming biography “The World Is Not Enough” and a professor and chair of the Department of English at Florida Atlantic University
Colin Burnett, program director of Film & Media Studies at Washington University in St. Louis, and author of the forthcoming book “James Bond and the Art of Franchise Storytelling”
James Chapman, the author of “Licence to Thrill: A Cultural History of the James Bond Films.”
Here’s what they had to say.
A ‘Surprise’ Casting
Pattinson came on late as a candidate after it was previously reported that actors Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult had all undergone screen tests for the role in October.

“I was surprised, to be honest,” Buckton tells TODAY.com. “I think like a lot of people, we had in mind a shortlist that didn’t include him. But having time to think about it, it does make sense in a number of ways.”
“My immediate reaction was, ‘Wow, I wasn’t really expecting that,’ and then I got really excited about the idea,” Chapman says.
“At no point in history has a major A-list star been cast as James Bond at the peak of their career.”
Colin Burnett said on what makes Pattinson's casting remarkable
Burnett called Pattinson’s casting “a tectonic shift” in the way the role has been filled in the past.

“At no point in history has a major A-list star been cast as James Bond at the peak of their career,” Burnett says. “They have had reasonable careers, but Pattinson is someone who comes in aware of his stardom, of his box office potential, of his performance, and who’s very much going to look forward to steering the franchise. None of the previous actors had the clout on the way in to do that.”
Why Robert Pattinson’s Casting Makes Sense
The recurring theme that came up as to why Pattinson got the nod is simple: box office dollars.

Amazon MGM Studios took creative control of the Bond franchise in 2025 after making a deal with the franchise’s longtime producers, Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. The change came four years after Amazon bought MGM, which owned the rights to the James Bond films, for $8.5 billion.

The online retail giant did not pay all that money to have the next Bond film to flop at the box office. That made going the traditional Bond route of casting an up-and-coming actor who is not yet widely known to the public, like Craig and former Bond actors Timothy Dalton and Pierce Brosnan, a gamble.

“I think that there’s so much at stake in this casting decision now with Amazon taking over and relaunching the whole franchise in a different way that they didn’t want to take a risk on an actor who hasn’t been in major films,” Buckton says.

“I know for a fact, having spoken to people inside Amazon, that they are hoping for and building the structure of Amazon MGM off a massive box office success (with Bond),” Burnett says. “What they’re hoping is to have a big hit right from the get-go, so that too is a major shift.”
Does Robert Pattinson Look the Part?

At 40, Pattinson is about the right age to play the superspy, who is generally considered to be in his late 30s, 40-ish in the Ian Fleming novels that made the character famous. The oldest actor to be cast as Bond was Roger Moore, who was 45 at the time.

Pattinson is also tall, lithe and dark-haired, which is closer to Fleming’s description of the character than Craig, who initially dealt with a wave of backlash about being blonde, short and muscular when he was first cast.
“People will feel just because of Pattinson’s look in a tuxedo with his hair back that he is James Bond, much more so than Daniel Craig,” Burnett says.
In an eerie coincidence, Pattinson resembles a cartoon rendering of Bond that Fleming had made in the late 1950s when he had a comic strip done of the character, according to Buckton.
“Fleming’s model was the 1930s star Hoagy Carmichael, but it looks uncannily like Robert Pattinson,” Buckton says.
Is Robert Pattinson Too Famous to Play Bond?
Will fans see James Bond on the screen or Robert Pattinson?

That is a question that has not been a problem for the six previous Bond actors, including the legendary Sean Connery, because they were not household names when they landed the role. The role made them famous.

“That’s the risk they’re taking, that he has too much baggage from other films,” Buckton says. “But he’s such a chameleon. Look at all the different roles he’s played, from ‘Twilight’ to ‘The Batman’ to movies like ‘The Lighthouse.’ I think they’re counting on him being able to do that again and reinvent himself as James Bond, and the fans will accept that.”
“The thing with Robert Pattinson is he changes with the times,” Burnett says. “He’s constantly reinventing himself.”

His experience in carrying big-budget films could actually be an asset rather than a drawback, according to the experts. It helps that he has already worked with director Denis Villeneuve on the “Dune” films because Villeneuve has committed to directing the next Bond film.

“He’s got that kind of crossover aspect to him,” Chapman says. “He’s done big franchise properties, big successful films with a female fanbase, so there’s real acting credentials there. He’s not a one-note actor. I’m thinking he can play Bond in a different way than he plays Batman.”
However, there’s also the possibility of overexposure if he’s also appearing in “Batman” and “Dune” movies in the midst of “Bond” films.

“Some of the negative reaction has been, let’s not have one actor taking on these iconic roles at the same time,” Buckton says. “That’s the risk, that Bond fans are like, ‘We want our own guy.  We want someone who’s not already Superman or Batman or whatever.’”
What Robert Pattinson Could Bring to the Role
Each of the previous six actors brought their own touch to the role, from the suave and sly Sean Connery to the campy Roger Moore to the brooding Daniel Craig.
Pattinson leaned in to a dark portrayal of Batman, so it remains to be seen how he balances the humor, physical prowess and romantic banter with the Bond girls in the new film.

“(Craig) became this wounded, dark, introspective James Bond, and I thought the new Bond would have to be a bit lighter,” Buckton says. “Even though (Pattinson) has played some dark characters, I think he has enough versatility. I would expect a little bit of a throwback to more of a suave, calm-under-pressure James Bond, and maybe a bit more of the Bond girl chemistry, which wasn’t Daniel Craig’s strong suit.”
“If Pattinson had come around and there had been no Craig, it would have been no problem to play more of a dark, psychological version, but Craig has cleared this ground already,” Burnett says.
Buckton speculated that maybe Pattinson’s performance in the Christopher Nolan movie “Tenet” could be a hint at what he does with Bond.
“I think that’s a glimpse of what he might be like because there’s something kind of edgy about him that I like, and maybe that’s what made him the choice,” he said.
Who Would Bond Experts Have Chosen?
Buckton liked “Superman” star Henry Cavill, 43, who was in the running for the role in the early 2000s as a 22-year-old but lost out to Craig.
Buckton would’ve gone with Callum Turner this time around.

“I could see him as Bond,” he says of Turner. “Some people say he didn’t have the charisma, but that’s something you can grow into. He could be identified as James Bond because he’s not a huge star right now, and I think he could bring that humor and a lighter touch to the role.”
Burnett would’ve gone with “Frankenstein” and “Wuthering Heights” star Jacob Elordi.

“I saw ‘Wuthering Heights’ in the theater and there’s a scene where he reemerges onscreen and the theater just swooned,” Burnett says. “That’s a star. That’s a thing Bond has always had. Men want to be like him and women want to be with him. Elordi has that feel.”

title: Walker Scobell Calls ‘Percy Jackson’ Season 3 ‘Most Accurate’ to the Books Yet
summary: Walker Scobell previews Season 3 of Disney+’s “Percy Jackson and the Olympians,” which will follow the events of “The Titan’s Curse” and majorly up the stakes.
story: Walker Scobell is ready for “The Titan’s Curse.” Percy Jackson, on the other hand, may not be.
“Be prepared,” Scobell tells TODAY.com. “It’s not like the other seasons... everything is a very real threat.”
With book and series fans alike anticipating Season 3 of “Percy Jackson and The Olympians,” set to release Nov. 20, the cast alludes to it as the series’ “darkest” addition yet.

Season 3 will follow the events of third book, “The Titan’s Curse.” With executive oversight by the series’ author, Rick Riordan, this will be the first time the third book has been adapted for the screen.

Riordan has been “involved in every writers room,” he told The Hollywood Reporter, much to the enthusiasm of book purists who were left disappointed by major changes in the Percy Jackson movie adaptations.

But Riordan isn’t the only one holding the TV adaptation to the book’s high standards. Scobell views the story from the perspective of its titular star and as a boy who first fell in love with the series at 9 years old.
“I would say it’s the most accurate season we’ve had, which was great for me,” Scobell tells TODAY.com.
To the 17-year-old, the more book-accurate the script is, the better.
“I almost sometimes wish I hadn’t read the books because, unfortunately, it’s hard for me to let it go,” he says.
“You know, there are things that have to change for (the show) to work,” he adds. “There’s also things that they’ve changed that have made it 10 times better.”
Previewing Season 3

“Percy Jackson and The Olympians” Season 3 will see Percy and an unlikely group of new characters journey across the country to find Annabeth (Leah Sava Jefferies) after she’s captured during their initial mission. Meanwhile, the threat of the demigod Luke (Charlie Bushnell), an impending war between the gods and titans and the great prophecy looms over Percy, who’s having to handle it all without Annabeth for the first time.
Like in previous seasons, this means viewers are in for plenty of epic showdowns — and on a grander scale than book readers may have originally envisioned, Scobell says.
“There are things we filmed that I was like, ‘Wow, this is so much bigger than it was in the books!’” he says.

It will also introduce some complicated new character dynamics, picking up with the cliffhanger at the end of Season 2. Thalia (Tamara Smart), the lost demigod daughter of Zeus, has returned to her human form after being turned into a tree years ago. This means that the great prophecy — which foretells that Olympus will be either saved or destroyed by a child of the big three gods (Zeus, Poseidon and Hades) — may not apply to Percy after all.

In the books, Percy and Thalia slowly establish a friendship, approaching each other with hesitancy but agreeableness. They also bond over the shared goal of saving Annabeth. But Scobell says that dynamic will look slightly different in Season 3, a change he says “works better” for the story’s arc.
“The only thing running through Percy’s head, in every single chapter in the book (is) ‘Annabeth, Annabeth, Annabeth,’” Scobell says.
In the show, Scobell’s character is driven by that same motivation, but the addition of Thalia adds “another level” of stakes to the quest.

“Now there’s this other girl, Thalia, who he doesn’t completely trust because they are so similar,” he adds. “It’s almost like he has to constantly choose what to focus on ... this ‘great prophecy’ with Thalia, or Annabeth.”
“I’m not going to spoil anything, but being so angry and intense at the beginning kind of carves out a nice story for the two of them,” he adds.

Thalia isn’t the only big three demigod Percy is going to have to look out for. “The Titan’s Curse” also famously introduces the di Angelo siblings, Bianca and Nico, to be played by Olive Abercrombie and and Levi Chrisopulos in Season 3. Fans of the book will remember that the Bianca and Nico turn out to be children of Hades.
“Levi, I mean ... he just looks like Nico,” Scobell says of his co-star. “Levi showed up, and he just kind of nailed it right away.”
As for how Percy will fare without Annabeth?
“Annabeth’s gone, yes, and her role in the trio ... she was the knowledgeable one on this whole world, right?” he says.

“You have Thalia and Grover, who have also had a lot of experience on the run,” he adds. “In a way, it’s kind of like that spot is, you know, not filled in, but there is someone there to to help make those decisions.”
More Star-Studded New Cast Members
Decisions, danger, and demigods aren’t the only things in store for our heroes. Another non-negotiable with quests? Run-ins with the gods of Olympus themselves, of course.

Joining the Olympian deities this season is Hera (Ming-Na Wen), Demeter (Jennifer Beals), Aphrodite (Kate McKinnon), Apollo (Hubert Smielecki) and Artemis (Dafne Keen). Season 3 will also be the first time since the show’s premiere that the gods will be seen altogether on Mount Olympus.
As intimidated as Percy is by the gods, so, too, was Scobell by his famous new co-stars.

“I had Jennifer Beals sign a ‘Flash Dance’ poster for me, and I had Ming-Na Wen sign a ‘Mulan’ poster for me,” Scobell says with a laugh. “That was the most nerve-wracking thing I think I’ve ever done on the set of ‘Percy Jackson.’”
What’s Next for Scobell?
As Season 3 debuts, Scobell is experiencing another life milestone: his junior year of high school.
“I don’t know if those two have ever really coincided very well,” he says.
“I don’t think I ever would have been able to do what I do without the help of my school, and then also the help of the set teachers I’ve been blessed with,” he adds.

As for what’s next, Scobell will appear in the upcoming “Angry Birds 3” movie, heading to theaters Dec. 23. He’s also hopeful for a “PJO” renewal for a fourth and fifth season. Scobell says the final two books in the series — “The Battle of the Labyrinth” and “The Last Olympian” — remain his favorites.
“I’ve always said (Book) 5, but you can’t really have the payoff of 5 without 4. So it’s like a ‘Avengers End Game—Infinity War’ situation,” Scobell says.
He also stresses that the show’s adaptation of “The Titan’s Curse” builds up the “intensity” that comes to a head in the final two parts of the story.

“There were points in filming the second and first season that I’m like, ‘I need to get hurt more,’ or like, ‘There needs to be a chance that I die on this quest,’” he says. “And with this, we’re narrowly escaping it every single time.”

title: Ukraine sinks Russian warship off Libya in latest expansion of the war
summary: Ukraine has taken its fight against Russia to the shores of North Africa, claiming to have sunk a warship off the coast of Libya in its latest expansion of the war.
story: Ukraine has taken its fight against Russia to the shores of North Africa, claiming to have sunk a warship off the coast of Libya in its latest expansion of the war.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday that Ukrainian naval drones had been used in the attack in the Mediterranean a day earlier, which came after Moscow said another of its ships was struck by drones in the Baltic Sea.
Zelenskyy shared footage of the attacks in a post on X, showing drones approaching several vessels followed by massive fireballs.
He said his forces deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones to sink the Russian corvette, Merkury, and hit a transport ship, the Angara, in an “exemplary Ukrainian operation.”
Ukraine’s Security Service, SBU, said the attacks took place near the Libyan port of Benghazi, some 1,500 miles from the established front lines of the conflict.

It said the corvette “regularly escorted enemy naval convoys” and in particular guarded the Angara cargo ship that was used to move weapons. “Both vessels were legitimate military targets for Ukraine, as they worked directly for Russia’s military capabilities,” the SBU said in a statement on Telegram.

Ukrainian uncrewed boats were delivered to a designated location and launched into the water from a so-called “mother ship,” the SBU said, reaching their targets despite “enemy’s attempts to destroy the Ukrainian drones from the air.” It said the Ka-27 multi-purpose helicopter was on board the corvette and was also sunk.
“The Defence Forces of Ukraine have once again shown that the Russian navy and its logistics have no safe routes, even far beyond the Black Sea,” the SBU added.
Ukraine noted that the ship was one of Russia’s newest, commissioned only in 2023.

Moscow has noted Zelenskyy’s “statement on this matter,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Monday when asked about the attacks. He deferred to the Russian Defense Ministry, which was yet to comment.
It’s the latest example of Kyiv launching surprise attacks to hit back against the Kremlin.
But the weekend attack caused fallout in Libya, where local authorities expressed outrage and the United Nations called for an independent probe.

The eastern Libya-based government said Sunday that an explosion took place aboard a Russian vessel docked at the Benghazi naval base. It said the vessel was en route back to Russia and had stopped at the port to refuel and take on supplies.
A comprehensive investigation into the attack will be launched, it said, in coordination with Russian authorities.

title: Crowd evacuated from U.S. rapper Don Toliver’s concert after ‘unknown substance’ released
summary: MANCHESTER, England — Thousands of people attending a concert of American rapper Don Toliver were evacuated from a major British arena Sunday evening, police said, after an “unknown substance” was released into the crowd.
story: MANCHESTER, England — Thousands of people attending a concert of American rapper Don Toliver were evacuated from a major British arena Sunday evening, police said, after an “unknown substance” was released into the crowd.
About 12,000 concertgoers were evacuated by emergency workers just after 10 p.m. local time (5 p.m. ET) from Toliver’s show at the Co-op Live venue in the northern English city of Manchester.
The North West Ambulance Service declared a major incident and​ said the substance was “believed to ​be tear gas” and was understood to ⁠have been released toward the ​end of the show.

“We deployed several emergency crews, including our Hazardous Area Response Team, to support the safe assessment and treatment of people at the scene,” it said in a statement, adding that one person had been hospitalized.
“More than 80 people were assessed by our clinicians, with some reporting eye and respiratory symptoms. Decontamination was carried out as a precaution,” the ambulance service said Monday.

People in the crowd were suffering effects “from an unknown substance,” Greater Manchester police said in its latest statement Monday. “Enquiries are underway into what the substance is and what caused the incident,” police added.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The venue, in the center of the busy city, was hosting Grammy Award-nominated R&B rapper-singer Toliver, whose real name is Caleb Zackery Toliver, as part of his Nitrous tour.

The Houston-based rapper is best known for hits “No idea” and “After Party,” and features on the soundtrack to the new “Grand Theft Auto VI” blockbuster game. Toliver has yet to publicly comment on the incident but is due to perform in London on Monday and Tuesday as part of his tour.
Manchester was left shaken in 2017 after a bombing at a nearby venue during an Ariana Grande concert left 22 people dead and made global headlines.

“We understand the concern that this incident will have raised,” Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker said Monday. “We will now begin to fully understand what this substance was and how this incident came about.”
“Several people were treated on site, and one has been taken to hospital at this time. Anyone who has left the event and since become unwell is advised to attend their local hospital,” Parker added.
Concertgoer Joey Howe, 22, told BBC Radio Manchester the lights came on and Toliver appeared to have been “rushed off stage.”

“I saw a lot of people streaming out and you go into this panic mode and you see a lot of people running out of the venue,” Howe said. He said people were “choking” and there was a “horrible smell” in the arena.
“It was just really distressing scenes and not something you want to see,” he added.
Another fan, Ben Stevenson, told the Manchester Evening News that he was in the standing section of the arena when he “started coughing and (my) eyes were kind of itchy.”
A spokesman for Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a former mayor of Manchester, called the incident “deeply worrying” and said the police would conduct a full investigation.
The venue, which opened in 2024, is due to host American singer Phoebe Bridgers on Thursday.

It said in a statement on X that it was “working closely with Greater Manchester Police to identify the cause and action appropriately. Our priority remains the safety and security of all visitors to Co-op Live, and we will provide more information once we have an update.”

title: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to kill Ukrainian American rapper on its soil
summary: COPENHAGEN, Denmark — Authorities thwarted the attempted killing of a Ukrainian American citizen on Danish soil in a plot allegedly orchestrated by Russian intelligence services, the Danish prime minister’s office said Friday.
story: COPENHAGEN, Denmark — Authorities thwarted the attempted killing of a Ukrainian American citizen on Danish soil in a plot allegedly orchestrated by Russian intelligence services, the Danish prime minister’s office said Friday.

The Russian defense attaché has been expelled from Denmark in response, Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen told a news conference. Two alleged members of the outlawed Danish gang “Loyal to Familia” have been arrested in connection with the attempted killing, police said.
Danish broadcaster DR, citing a court hearing, reported the men are suspected of having been recruited to assassinate ​a Ukrainian rapper ahead of a planned performance.
Police thwarted the alleged plot when they arrested ​the two men shortly before the rapper ​Kyivstoner’s Sept. 25 concert, which was later ⁠canceled.

It was unclear how police identified the two men, who ​were stopped in ​a vehicle ⁠carrying several weapons, or how the investigation expanded to include two other men ​who are not accused of participating ​in ⁠the alleged assassination plot targeting Kyivstoner.
However, all four men have been held in custody since September, according to ⁠the ​broadcaster.
It was also unclear how ​the Russian intelligence services allegedly recruited the two Danish suspects.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said: “It is a clear illustration of the grave security situation Denmark and Europe find ourselves in. We are facing a Russia under pressure which is acting more aggressively and is more willing to take risks.”

The Danes’ announcement came as tensions between Europe and Russia heightened again Friday. Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland in what its prime minister said was likely a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine.
European Commission ​President Ursula von der Leyen said on Saturday the E.U. ⁠stands in full solidarity with Denmark.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“This was an ​attack ⁠on E.U. ‌soil. And it is unacceptable. We stand in full ‌solidarity with Denmark. ‌And with all Member States targeted by Russian ⁠hybrid attacks,” she said in an X post.
European Council President António Costa said: “We will not be intimidated. Russia’s tactics and threats will not weaken the European Union’s resolve to continue supporting Ukraine.”
The Russian Embassy in Copenhagen said on Friday the accusations were not backed ‌with proof.

title: Trump calling Putin ‘my friend’ at APEC summit sparks backlash
summary: When President Donald Trump called Vladimir Putin his “friend” this week, European leaders and foreign policy experts were dismayed and alarmed.
story: Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, is wanted by the International Criminal Court on allegations of war crimes, and is accused of overseeing a yearslong campaign of election interference, sabotage and cyberattacks against the West.

So when President Donald Trump pointed to the Russian leader and declared, “He’s my friend,” at the historic Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China on Thursday, the reaction from some of America’s closest European allies was one of alarm and disbelief.
“God, protect us from such friends,” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk posted to X shortly afterward.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“The optics of embracing Putin and calling him a friend cause us some concern,” Poland’s foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, told a news conference Thursday. He added that it posed the question of whom Trump considered a closer friend, Putin or Poland, and “if push came to shove, which friend would he choose?”

Their comments came hours before Poland’s defense minister, Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, accused Russia of violating the country’s airspace overnight with three objects that were probably two missiles and a drone. Elsewhere, Estonia said it would close its road border crossings with Russia on security grounds for at least six months.

Much of the criticism of Trump’s remark has come from Poland, historically one of Washington’s closest allies in Europe but whose officials have grown increasingly wary of Trump’s dealings with Russia. The country, which borders Ukraine, Russia and Moscow’s close ally Belarus, has long been among the most outspoken European governments warning about the threat of Russian aggression. Its security strategy also relies heavily on the United States and NATO.
More broadly, the word “friend” also caused fresh alarm among other European governments, some of which are openly warning that Putin may expand his aggression beyond Ukraine and attack them, too.

Ultimately, there is widespread concern that elevating Putin alongside Trump and China’s Xi Jinping will legitimize and embolden a leader whom Western governments have sought to isolate over his record of grave human rights abuses and aggression against other countries, allegations he has routinely denied.

The joint declaration made by Trump, Putin and Xi after their meeting made no mention of Ukraine but condemned the International Criminal Court, which has issued a warrant for Putin’s arrest over the alleged unlawful deportation of Ukrainian children to Russia.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said it was “very incomprehensible” that Trump would meet with Putin, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz was among those who warned against the meeting becoming a rerun of the Yalta Conference of 1945. The summit toward the end of World War II saw President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin effectively carve up occupied Germany and other parts of Europe.

Others, including British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, were more restrained. Asked whether Trump had “fallen for Putin’s charm offensive,” he replied that it was “quite the opposite” and that Trump had “talked about the horrific loss of life, including the loss of young Russian lives, and he spoke quite passionately about that subject.”
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte also defended the principle of nuclear powers meeting to pursue diplomacy.
Burnham and Rutte were speaking at a meeting in Berlin of the “Coalition of the Willing,” a group of nearly 40 countries working to support Ukraine and provide security guarantees.
They were joined by Steve Witkoff and Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, the U.S. envoys tasked with brokering peace between Moscow and Kyiv.

Trump called into a meeting of dozens of European leaders and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Thursday, telling the group that Putin was ready to end the war, according to five European officials briefed on the discussions. He also encouraged the Europeans to make a deal so they can stop spending money on Ukraine and spend it on their own countries, the officials said.
Kushner also mentioned the call in a post on X but said it was up to the president to reveal what he said.

“Trump wants to make a deal with Europe by his side. He’s not looking to impose anything unilaterally,” Kushner said. “Any deal we do will be in close consultation with Ukraine and with Europe. That’s something that he also asked us to come here today and reassure people in that regard.”

The White House did not immediately respond to an overnight request for comment on the criticisms about Trump’s comment about Putin. But Trump defended his description of the Russian president in an interview with Reuters, saying that “it’s nice to have people that have 4,000 nuclear weapons as a friend as opposed to an enemy.”

This is far from the first time Trump has spoken warmly about Putin, joking in 2013 about becoming his “new best friend.” Once in office, Trump said in 2018 that the pair “got on very well,” and in 2022, he described Putin’s initial moves against Ukraine as “genius” and “savvy.” In 2023 and again in 2024, Trump recounted telling Putin, “We’re friends.”
However, this week was the first time Trump made the declaration to Putin’s face, in front of television cameras at one of the most hotly anticipated meetings of recent years.

“It’s one thing to say in an interview, ‘We get on,’ as Trump has in the past; it’s quite another to see him crossing a room in the hotel in China with an effusive smile on his face and gushing about ‘my friend,’” said Jonathan Eyal, international director of the Royal United Services Institute, a London-based think tank. “It all felt very natural and very real.”

Mara Karlin, who was assistant secretary of defense for strategy, plans and capabilities under President Joe Biden, told NBC News that while Trump’s past actions on Greenland and Ukraine have provoked outcry, “referring to Putin as a ‘friend’ seems to evoke a visceral reaction because it is both entirely believable and inconceivable for any other American president to embrace a Russian leader so literally.”
The condemnation was not confined to one side of the Atlantic.

In the United States, Democrats were openly scathing. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer of New York called Trump’s words “embarrassing, despicable, and quite frankly pathetic,” while Sen. Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, described Trump’s “friend” as a “murderous war criminal.”

Sen. Mark Kelly of Arizona said: “Putin is not my friend. He’s not your friend. He’s not a friend of this country, and when the president of the United States refers to him in that way, it emboldens him.”
Republicans were more circumspect. Sen. Rick Scott of Florida called Putin a “thug” but acknowledged that Trump needed to work with him.

Bill Browder, a British American financier who spearheaded the international campaign for Russian sanctions and has become one of Putin’s most prominent critics, also described his “revulsion and disgust” at hearing Trump’s words.

“He’s a guy who’s a geopolitical menace, and he should not get any kind of respect, let alone from the American head of state,” Browder told NBC News in a telephone interview. “To be elevated to the top table with genuine superpowers is an unbelievable symbolic position to sit in.”

When asked about Trump’s comment at the end of the news conference following the “Coalition of the Willing” meeting in the German capital, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy only shrugged and walked offstage.

title: Iraqi security forces deploy in Iran-backed militia stronghold
summary: JURF AL-SAKHAR, Iraq — Iraqi security forces deployed in Jurf al-Sakhar, a stronghold of the Kataib Hezbollah armed group, on Friday under a deal that seeks to limit the reach of Iran’s most powerful Shi’ite militia ally in the country without provoking a confrontation.
story: JURF AL-SAKHAR, Iraq — Iraqi security forces deployed in Jurf al-Sakhar, a stronghold of the Kataib Hezbollah armed group, on Friday under a deal that seeks to limit the reach of Iran’s most powerful Shi’ite militia ally in the country without provoking a confrontation.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi this week ordered security forces to move against the heavily armed Kataib Hezbollah, which officials accused of running an oil smuggling network siphoning state-owned oil worth hundreds of millions of dollars in Jurf al-Sakhar.

The hardline Kataib Hezbollah (Battalions of the Party of God), branded a terrorist group by the United States, has rejected the smuggling accusations, which have led to arrests that prompted fears of an armed response. The group is among those that have claimed attacks on US forces in Gulf states since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran.

A convoy of vehicles flying Iraqi flags headed into Jurf al-Sakhar on Friday and soldiers took up positions in the center after senior security officials told a press conference that government forces would protect the town.
Members of the Kataib Hezbollah group stood near their group’s flags.

“From Jurf al-Sakhar, we begin asserting state authority across all of Iraq, confronting corruption and weapons beyond state control,” Zaidi told government troops who entered the town, speaking from a military operations center in Baghdad.
“Our decision is firm: No weapons outside state authority, no weapons but Iraq‘s, no decisions but Iraq‘s, and no flag shall fly higher than the Iraqi flag.”
Under the arrangement, brokered by Shi’ite politicians, Kataib members were expected to withdraw to other parts of Iraq, a major oil producer and ally of both the US and Iran.
“God willing, things will be safe and secure with the presence of the security forces,” said resident Mohamed Ali.
Senior Iranian representative visited Baghdad, sources say

The deal will include the opening of a security headquarters in Jurf al-Sakhar on Saturday to oversee the handover. Iraq‘s energy police have begun securing an oil pipeline in Jurf al-Sakhar, the state news agency reported.

“Today is a historic moment in which the Iraqi Armed Forces prove that they are the nation’s shield, safety valve, and the guardian ensuring security stability for the Iraqi people,” Sabah al-Numan, spokesperson for the commander-in-chief of the Iraqi armed forces, told the press conference.

Reflecting the sensitivity of the situation, Iraqi Shi’ite political figures said Esmail Qaani, commander of Iran’s Revolutionary Guards’ Quds Force, arrived in Baghdad on Monday to help defuse tensions with Kataib Hezbollah.
So far, nine senior security and oil officials have been dismissed following an investigation focused on Jurf al-Sakhar in Babil province, about 50 km (30 miles) south of Baghdad.
Any direct confrontation with Iran’s heavily armed militia allies in Iraq could be risky.

After one of Zaidi’s predecessors ordered a similar crackdown on those armed groups five years ago, the prime minister’s Baghdad home was hit in a drone strike that authorities described at the time as an assassination attempt.
Refusal to disarm

US President Donald Trump has pressured Zaidi to disarm the militias that have struck US troops and facilities in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates in solidarity with Tehran since the US and Israel launched attacks on Iran in February.
Kataib Hezbollah and other militias, all of whom report directly to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, have refused to hand over their weapons to the state.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Founded in the aftermath of the 2003 US-led invasion of Iraq, Kataib is among the most influential members of the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, the umbrella group of hardline Shi’ite armed organisations supported by Iran.

Kataib Hezbollah quickly developed a reputation for deadly attacks against military and diplomatic targets during the US-led counterinsurgency war and sectarian conflict of the 2000s, using snipers, rockets, mortars and roadside bombs.
Wide Iranian sway in Iraq

Since the 2003 US-led invasion toppled Iran’s arch-enemy, longtime Sunni leader Saddam Hussein, Tehran has steadily expanded its influence in Iraq through close ties with heavily armed Shi’ite militias and political parties.

Iraqi security officials say the militias’ arsenals include assault rifles, machineguns, anti-tank guided missiles, mortars, precision-guided rockets, armed drones and some short-range ballistic and cruise missile capabilities.

Kataib has its own political party, called Huquq, or Rights, with five lawmakers. An Iraqi official report said the group also generates cash through businesses such as construction, housing, trade, tourism and currency exchange, though Kataib denies this and says it is dedicated to security.

Pro-Iranian militias, including Kataib, enjoy a semi-official status in Iraq, which critics say encourages them to act with impunity. A shadowy group with no announced leadership structure, Kataib Hezbollah has thousands of hardened fighters.
It forms several battalions in Iraq‘s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), a grouping of armed factions set up in 2014 to fight Islamic State and subsequently recognized as an official security force.

Fighters receive state salaries and Kataib Hezbollah members, including some designated as terrorists by the US, hold senior positions in the PMF. While it is technically under the command of Iraq‘s prime minister as part of the PMF, the group often operates outside the chain of command.

title: Deadly Russian strikes hit 3 Kyiv bridges after Putin vows revenge for Crimea attacks
summary: Three bridges in Kyiv were hit in a Russian ballistic missile attack, officials in the Ukrainian capital said, after President Vladimir Putin vowed revenge.
story: KYIV, Ukraine — Three bridges in Kyiv were hit Friday in a massive Russian ballistic missile attack, officials in the Ukrainian capital said, hours after President Vladimir Putin vowed “painful” revenge for strikes on his prized bridge linking Crimea to Russia.

The attacks, which started in the early hours of the morning and continued well into the day, damaged the Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges connecting the left and right banks of the Dnipro River, which flows through the city, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said in a post on Telegram.

At least six people were killed and 15 injured in those strikes, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said in a separate post. Two others were killed in separate attacks across the country, which saw nine regions hit overnight, he said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The strikes on Kyiv forced authorities to restrict traffic on the bridges, impacting the movement across the capital. Klitschko asked residents not to drive private cars into the city “unless absolutely necessary” and suggested employers let staff work remotely.
Russia has been hitting Kyiv’s Southern and Northern bridges since early October, causing multiple closures, disrupting metro services and causing traffic jams.
But it is the first time that Russia hit three different bridges in a single night, and it has left most of the main road crossings over the Dnipro simultaneously damaged or restricted.
An NBC News team in Kyiv heard air raid sirens going off every few minutes overnight, accompanied by loud explosions.
After dawn broke on the rainy and foggy Friday morning, firefighters were seen putting out the flames from a strike on an industrial area in the capital.
It’s part of the daily reality for Kyiv’s residents after Russia escalated both the number of ballistic missiles it was firing at the capital and the frequency of attacks.
The latest strikes came hours after Putin said that Moscow would retaliate after Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia and Crimea for a third time this week.

title: Trump urges nuclear arms control in historic meeting with Putin and Xi
summary: What these three men might decide has the potential to reverberate across the globe.
story: SHENZHEN, China — It’s unclear what decisions may come from this historic meeting.
But the spectacle of President Donald Trump’s meeting with Russia’s Vladimir Putin and China’s Xi Jinping may be what delivers the defining image.

On Thursday, Trump, Putin and Xi met on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen. Sitting around a huge, doughnut-shaped table at the Kylin Villa resort were leaders of three of the world’s most powerful nations: the U.S. with its largest economy, Russia with its biggest nuclear arsenal, and China its largest standing army and manufacturing sector.
“We are really making history,” Trump said.

The sight of Trump expressing such warmth toward two authoritarian strongmen will have left many American allies outside the room dismayed. After Trump called Putin his “friend,” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk posted to X, “God, protect us from such friends.” Russia has invaded Ukraine and waged a yearslong campaign of sabotage, cyberattacks and misinformation against the West.
Others were concerned about the prospect of a “Yalta 2.0,” a reprise of the 1945 Yalta Conference in which the U.S., Britain and the then-Soviet Union met to carve up the postwar world.
After Thursday’s meeting finished, Russia and China issued a brief statement that was light on detail or major announcements. The U.S. did not immediately release a version.

The “China-Russia-U.S. Declaration on Peace” agreed to “reform” the United Nations “so that it can more effectively respond to global challenges.” (Russia and China have long sought to shift the body away from Western human rights concerns, while Trump has been a strident critic of the world body.) The declaration agreed to boost the production and supply of petroleum products, which have been disrupted by the Ukraine and Iran wars, and it rebuked the International Criminal Court not to abuse its power. (The ICC has issued an arrest warrant for Putin.)
The final point was that the leaders vowed to take steps to avoid nuclear war, although no specifics were mentioned.

The last remaining treaty between Washington and Moscow, New START, lapsed in February, but China, which has a far smaller nuclear arsenal than the other two, has resisted calls to be included in a new agreement.

“As the world’s three largest nuclear powers, by far, the United States, Russia, and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth, and to lessen the risk that those weapons will ever be used,” Trump said in the public section of the meeting.
“Once you have the nuclear weapons, it’s very hard to not have them, it’s very hard to give them up,” he added. “That’s the way life works.”

title: Palestinians flee as Israeli tanks cross Gaza ceasefire’s ‘yellow line’
summary: Israel’s ground operation across the yellow ceasefire line in Gaza, which forced Palestinians to flee their makeshift shelters, marks a fresh escalation in the conflict and risks undermining an already floundering truce with Hamas, analysts said Thursday.
story: Israel’s ground operation across the yellow ceasefire line in Gaza, which forced Palestinians to flee their makeshift shelters, marks a fresh escalation in the conflict and risks undermining an already floundering truce with Hamas, analysts said Thursday.

As tanks rolled into central Gaza on Wednesday, residents could be seen carrying blankets and other belongings away from their tents in pictures and video taken shortly after the Israeli military began what it said was an operation targeting a “terror tunnel.”

Others could be seen rolling away mattresses on carts and pushing loved ones in wheelchairs away from the scene near the Nuseirat camp in central Gaza. At least one person was reported to have been killed in an Israeli airstrike near the raid, Palestinian medics said, according to Reuters.

“Bullets were fired at us,” Amna al-Gasar, 49, told NBC News after she fled the scene with her young children, her baby in a pink fluffy sweater strapped to her chest. She said her family had received “evacuation orders” from the Israeli military and that tanks had advanced on the area.

“This is the 14th time that we’re getting displaced,” al-Gasar said, who added that she is from Gaza City in the north of the enclave which is now on the side of the “yellow line” occupied by Israeli forces. “Where should we go? We are exhausted. This is not a life,” she said.

Muna Abu Shehadeh, 37, said in a separate interview that along with some of her relatives, she left “with nothing but our children — no bedding, no food, and no water.” She added that she had a daughter who was ill, as well as a baby, and that they had to leave behind what few supplies they had.

The Israeli military told NBC News the ground operation was the first to be executed beyond the yellow line — the boundary marking the roughly 60% of Gaza that remains occupied by Israeli forces — since the U.S.-brokered ceasefire with Hamas came into effect in October 2025.

Separately, in a joint statement with the Israel Security Agency, or Shin Bet, the Israel Defense Forces said the operation was a “targeted” assault aimed at dismantling a tunnel that “posed an immediate and direct threat” to troops.

title: Trump pushes for three-way nuclear deal as Russia and China show little interest
summary: President Donald Trump has repeatedly placed nonproliferation near the top of the agenda for his unprecedented trilateral meeting Thursday with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, but his counterparts have expressed little interest in committing to new limitations on their nuclear arsenals.
story: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump has repeatedly placed nonproliferation near the top of the agenda for his trilateral meeting Thursday with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, although his counterparts have expressed little interest in committing to new limitations on their nuclear arsenals.

Trump has been pushing for China to join the U.S. and Russia in a new nuclear arms control agreement since his first term in office. Still, he has sought to limit expectations for any major progress in Shenzhen, China, where the world’s top three nuclear powers are meeting on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders.

Russia suspended its participation in New START, its last remaining nuclear arms pact with the U.S., when it invaded Ukraine in 2022, denying inspections of its nuclear sites. Ahead of the treaty’s expiration this past February, Russia said it would keep to the deal’s limitations on its arsenal for another year, but Trump insisted a new agreement must include China and possibly other nuclear powers.

China has said an arms control agreement should remain between the U.S. and Russia, which together hold nearly 90% of the world’s nuclear arsenal, with more than 5,000 warheads each. China has about 600, according to Pentagon estimates, though by 2030 it could have up to 1,000 if its arsenal continues to expand at the current rate.

“China is building up its nuclear arsenal to a very significant degree, and it will continue to do so, and wants to continue to do so,” David Sacks, a senior fellow for Asia studies at the Council on Foreign Relations, told reporters Wednesday.

The Chinese foreign ministry has declined to say whether nuclear arms control will be discussed at the trilateral meeting on Thursday, with spokesperson Mao Ning saying earlier this week that the three leaders “will have an in-depth exchange of views on important issues bearing on global peace.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

In a call last week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi “agreed on the importance of meaningful leader-level conversations to advance goals such as peace and denuclearization,” according to a U.S. readout of the call. The Chinese readout made no reference to such a discussion.
Trump has admitted that it will be difficult to get Russia and China to consider reducing their nuclear arsenals.

“So we’re going to talk about denuclearization. Tough subject because it’s very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes, right? But especially since you do have other countries,” he said Monday. “But we’re going to be talking about denuclearization.”

Even in the hours leading up to this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, the world’s top two nuclear powers were making shows of force. On Tuesday, the U.S. launched an unarmed intercontinental ballistic missile in a previously unannounced test at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. Hours later, Russia landed two strategic bombers in Vietnam to coincide with Putin’s arrival in China.

While one meeting is not likely to produce dramatic breakthroughs, it could kick-start a process that leads to sustained, formal bilateral or multilateral negotiations on nuclear risk reduction, arms control and disarmament, said Daryl Kimball, executive director of the Washington-based Arms Control Association.

“A top priority for all three leaders should be to head off a costly, escalatory nuclear arms race involving the further buildup of nuclear forces and the resumption of nuclear testing by any state,” he said.

Da Wei, director of the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University in Beijing, said nuclear arms control was not a “proper topic” for the trilateral meeting given the complexity of the issue and how little time Trump, Putin and Xi will have together.
But if the three leaders “can say something about nuclear stability, like a nuclear war is not winnable and should not be fought, I think that will be helpful,” he said in an interview Wednesday.
Rubio has acknowledged that a new agreement could take some time.

“Past agreements, including New START, took years to negotiate and were built upon decades of precedent. They were also between two powers, not three or more,” he wrote on Substack in February. “However, just because something is hard does not mean we should not pursue it or settle for less.”

title: Xi greets Trump as he arrives in China, a rare move ahead of Putin talks
summary: In a rare and surprising move, Chinese leader Xi Jinping personally greeted President Donald Trump as he arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of historic three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
story: SHENZHEN, China — In a rare and surprising move, Chinese leader Xi Jinping personally greeted President Donald Trump as he arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of historic three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
It is believed to be the first time that Xi, in power for more than a decade, has been on hand to greet any foreign leader arriving in China.

He was reciprocating the personal greeting he had received from Trump in September, when the American leader met him at the plane upon his arrival for a White House state visit. Lawmakers from both parties had criticized Trump over the move, which is also rare for U.S. presidents.

A report by Xinhua, China’s state-run news agency, said that during Trump’s arrival in the city of Shenzhen on Wednesday, Xi noted the special trip the American president and first lady Melania Trump had made to welcome him at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington.
“China is a nation that values courtesy and has a tradition of returning goodwill with goodwill,” the Xinhua report said.

After Trump descended from Air Force One, a handshake between the two leaders turned into a quick hug as rows of military regiments and performers wearing bright pink and turquoise outfits stood at attention. A martial band played the American and Chinese national anthems as dancers waved flowers, pompoms and Chinese and American flags.

title: Meghan Markle’s father faces new child sex abuse complaints in the Philippines
summary: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, was charged with the possession of child abuse material, police in the Philippines said.
story: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, has had criminal complaints filed against him over alleged online child sexual abuse offences, police in the Philippines said Wednesday.

The complaints accuse Markle of violating local laws against online sexual abuse and exploitation of children, police told Reuters. They added that the complaints were filed before the prosecutor’s office in Cebu on Monday, following an investigation last month into the alleged distribution and possession of child sexual abuse materials.
Markle had lived in Cebu for a period before returning to the United States.

Prosecutors the evaluating the charges filed by police before they decide whether to issue a subpoena against Markle whose legal team would have 10 days to respond with a counter-affidavit. Prosecutors would then decide whether to proceed with a court case.
Prince Harry and Meghan’s spokesperson declined to comment when NBC News asked about the latest charges.

The announcement came less than two weeks after the 82-year-old was arrested in Florida and charged with one count of possession of child pornography, according to a criminal complaint filed by the Justice Department.

The FBI seized around 78 items from two storage units rented by Markle in Los Angeles, that contained “suspected child pornography,” according to court documents. Items seized include film negatives featuring an adult man with naked “pre-pubescent” girls, the complaint said, which added that a witness “positively identified the adult man as Markle.”
Based on background in one photo, the FBI determined the images found in California were taken in a hotel in the Philippines, according to the court document.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Markle was taken into custody in Tampa, Florida, and was later released under house arrest.
But after he cut off his ankle monitor, a federal judge ordered last week that Markle remain in custody for violating the conditions of his release.

Markle had been living in a senior care facility in Lakeland, Florida after he was forced to return to the U.S. from the Philippines when he suffered a stroke and a leg was amputated, according to The Associated Press.
The retired television lighting and photography director denied the allegations last month, calling them “sick lies.”

Meghan Markle asaid in a statement last month that she was “deeply distressed” by the allegations against her father. Their relationship has been limited and fraught in recent years, with her father not attending her wedding to Harry in 2018 amid widespread media scrutiny.

Her statement said that she was previously informed of “disturbing allegations” against him, with British police subsequently confirming she was passed a letter in January 2019 “containing a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom.”

London’s Metropolitan Police said it had not informed other law enforcement agencies about the allegations in the letter at the time, referring itself to Britain’s policing watchdog over the handling of the allegations.

“The breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine,” said Meghan, who said she had chosen to keep her children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, away from her father “for one reason: to protect them.”
Meghan Markle and her husband, Prince Harry, stepped back as working royals in 2020 amid widespread reports of a royal rift and moved to, leaving Britain for California.

Harry, the second son of King Charles III and the late Princess Diana, leveled harsh criticism at Buckingham Palace and other senior royals across a series of media interviews and a tell-all memoir, “Spare.”
The couple returned to Britain two months ago, with their two children moving to schools in the country.

title: A Kremlin trap? Europe sees danger in Vladimir Putin’s new demand in U.S. talks
summary: European leaders have long feared being frozen out of U.S.-Russia peace talks about Ukraine. Now  Trump’s team negotiating the continent’s security structure.
story: LONDON — When European nations said they wanted greater involvement in Ukraine peace talks, this was almost certainly not what they had in mind.

Europe has long demanded more say in negotiations to end Russia’s war, fearful of being frozen out by Washington and Moscow. They dread a deal favorable to President Vladimir Putin — who will meet President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at a historic three-way meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday.

The good news for them is that the United States says it is now pushing to include Europe in the next rounds of diplomacy. The bad news, say governments, officials and foreign policy analysts, is the alarming new suggestion from Trump’s team: that the entire future of European security should be up for discussion too  — the same demand that Putin has pushed for years.

To the Russian leader, redrawing Europe’s security map means scaling back NATO’s presence, righting what he perceives as the injustices imposed on Moscow after the Soviet Union’s collapse. A succession of senior European officials have lambasted the idea, warning that Washington risks “walking into Moscow’s trap,” as Kaja Kallas, the European Union’s foreign policy chief, put it.
“This is all rather bizarre,” former Estonian President Toomas Hendrik Ilves said, summing up this sentiment in an interview with NBC News on Monday.

It’s not clear how or why the U.S. came to float a maximalist demand that Putin first made in 2021, one that was widely rejected by Western governments months before Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. But in recent days, as Washington ups its pressure for a breakthrough in peace talks, Russia and the U.S. have both revived the idea.
Jared Kushner, the president’s son-in-law and envoy, wrote Friday that talks should tackle the “broader postwar European security arrangements.”
